topic: Classification & Structural Behavior of Water Tanks
question: Differentiate between underground tanks, ground tanks, and overhead tanks based on loading and structural behavior.
solution:
1. Primary Structural & Loading Distinctions (IS 3370):
  • Underground Water Tanks:
    • Applied Loads: External lateral earth pressure ($p_e = K_a \gamma_s h$), surcharge loads, internal hydrostatic water pressure ($p_w = \gamma_w h$), and critical uplift water table pressure on bottom slab ($p_u = \gamma_w h_w$).
    • Critical Design Cases: Tank full with no soil outside (maximum hoop/bursting tension) AND Tank empty with saturated soil backfill to ground level (maximum compressive hoop & bending moments).
    • Structural Behavior: Walls span vertically as propped cantilevers (fixed at base raft, hinged/propped by roof slab) or horizontally as continuous closed rectangular frames.
  • Ground Water Tanks (Resting on Ground):
    • Applied Loads: Internal hydrostatic water pressure ($p = \gamma_w h$) and foundation base reaction ($q = \frac{W_{total}}{A}$).
    • Critical Design Cases: Tank full condition dominates; foundation soil provides uniform upward support without lateral passive restraint.
    • Structural Behavior: Circular walls experience pure hoop tension with flexible base; cantilever shear and vertical bending develop near base if wall-to-base joint is rigid/pinned.
  • Overhead Water Tanks (Elevated Tanks):
    • Applied Loads: Hydrostatic pressure, self-weight of domes/walls/ring girders, severe lateral environmental forces (wind pressure per IS 875 Part 3 and seismic inertial forces per IS 1893 Part 2).
    • Critical Design Cases: Tank full under maximum lateral wind/earthquake shear AND tank empty under maximum overturning moment.
    • Structural Behavior: Superstructure acts as membrane shell structure; staging (columns + braces or shaft) behaves as cantilever space frame transferring lateral shears and axial thrusts to pile/raft foundation.
Eg Intze elevated tanks in municipal water supplies balance top outward thrust against bottom inward conical thrust, whereas underground metro station sump tanks resist continuous hydrostatic groundwater uplift.

topic: Underground Rectangular Water Tank Design
question: Design wall elements of underground rectangular water tank of dimensions 5 m * 3 m * 3.5 m with free board of 0.3 m using any design method. Draw R/F details also. Use M30 grade of concrete and Fe 500 steel.
solution:
1. Design Data & Geometric Proportions:
  • Plan Dimensions: Length $L = 5\text{ m}$, Width $B = 3\text{ m}$; Total Height $H = 3.5\text{ m}$; Freeboard $FB = 0.3\text{ m}$
  • Effective Water Depth: $h = H - FB = 3.5 - 0.3 = 3.2\text{ m}$
  • Materials: M30 concrete ($f_{ck} = 30\text{ N/mm}^2$, $\sigma_{ct} = 1.5\text{ N/mm}^2$, $\sigma_{cbc} = 10\text{ N/mm}^2$) and Fe 500 steel ($f_y = 500\text{ N/mm}^2$, $\sigma_{st} = 130\text{ N/mm}^2$ on liquid face per IS 3370:2009 working stress / limit state crack width $\le 0.1\text{ mm}$)
  • Aspect Ratio: $\frac{L}{B} = \frac{5}{3} = 1.67 < 2.0 \implies$ Walls behave as a continuous horizontal frame in upper section, while lower section acts as vertical cantilever fixed at base raft.
2. Loading & Structural Analysis:
  • Height of cantilever portion: $h_c = 1.0\text{ m}$ or $\frac{H}{4} = \frac{3.5}{4} = 0.875\text{ m}$. Adopt $h_c = 1.0\text{ m}$ from base.
  • Height of horizontal frame portion: $H - h_c = 3.5 - 1.0 = 2.5\text{ m}$.
  • Maximum hydrostatic pressure for horizontal frame at depth $y = 2.5\text{ m}$: $$p = \gamma_w \cdot y = 10 \times 2.5 = 25\text{ kN/m}^2$$
  • Fixed End Moments for continuous frame ($L = 5\text{ m}, B = 3\text{ m}$): $$M_F(AB) = -\frac{p L^2}{12} = -\frac{25 \times 5^2}{12} = -52.08\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$ $$M_F(BC) = +\frac{p B^2}{12} = +\frac{25 \times 3^2}{12} = +18.75\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Moment Distribution at corner joint gives Corner Support Moment: $$M_{corner} \approx \frac{p (L^2 + B^2)}{24} = \frac{25 (25 + 9)}{24} = \frac{850}{24} = 35.42\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Maximum Mid-span Moments: $$M_{mid, L} = \frac{p L^2}{8} - M_{corner} = \frac{25 \times 25}{8} - 35.42 = 78.13 - 35.42 = 42.71\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$ $$M_{mid, B} = \frac{p B^2}{8} - M_{corner} = \frac{25 \times 9}{8} - 35.42 = 28.13 - 35.42 \implies \text{No positive moment; net hogging at corner governs.}$$
  • Direct Tension in Walls: $$T_L = p \cdot \frac{B}{2} = 25 \times 1.5 = 37.5\text{ kN/m}$$ $$T_B = p \cdot \frac{L}{2} = 25 \times 2.5 = 62.5\text{ kN/m}$$
3. Section Sizing & Reinforcement Design:
  • Wall Thickness: Limiting tensile stress criteria on uncracked section ($d \approx \sqrt{\frac{M}{Q \cdot b}}$): $$t_{wall} \ge \sqrt{\frac{6 \times 42.71 \times 10^6}{1000 \times 1.5}} \approx 413\text{ mm} \implies \text{Adopt overall thickness } D = 350\text{ mm with } d = 300\text{ mm}$$
  • Corner Negative Steel (Inside face): $$A_{st, corner} = \frac{M - T \cdot x}{\sigma_{st} \cdot j \cdot d} + \frac{T}{\sigma_{st}} = \frac{35.42 \times 10^6}{130 \times 0.85 \times 300} + \frac{62.5 \times 10^3}{130} = 1068 + 481 = 1549\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 16 mm dia bars @ 125 mm c/c ($A_{st} = 1608\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$).
  • Mid-span Long Wall Steel (Outside face): $$A_{st, mid} = \frac{42.71 \times 10^6}{130 \times 0.85 \times 300} + \frac{37.5 \times 10^3}{130} = 1288 + 288 = 1576\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 16 mm dia bars @ 125 mm c/c.
  • Vertical Cantilever Steel (Bottom 1 m): $$M_{cant} = \frac{1}{6} \gamma_w h_c^3 = \frac{1}{6} \times 10 \times 1.0^3 = 1.67\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m} \implies \text{Governed by minimum steel } 0.24\% = 840\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 12 mm dia vertical bars @ 130 mm c/c on both faces.
Eg Critical detail: provide a 150 mm x 150 mm interior haunch at all 4 corners with diagonal 16 mm ties to resist corner splitting under high hydrostatic corner moments.

topic: Design Procedure for Fixed Base Circular Tank
question: Outline the design steps for a circular cylindrical tank resting on ground with rigid/fixed base conditions.
solution:
1. Step-by-Step Design Protocol (IS 3370 Part IV):
  • Step 1: Geometric Dimensioning & Ratio Formulation:
    • Select diameter ($D$) and water height ($H$) based on storage capacity $V = \frac{\pi}{4} D^2 H$.
    • Compute IS 3370 dimension parameter: $\frac{H^2}{D \cdot t}$ (initially assume trial thickness $t \approx 30 H + 50\text{ mm}$).
  • Step 2: Analysis of Internal Actions (IS 3370 Table 9 & 10 Coefficients):
    • Fixed base prevents radial dilation and angular rotation $\implies$ load is partitioned into hoop tension $T(y)$ and vertical cantilever bending moment $M(y)$.
    • Compute maximum hoop tension: $T_{max} = \text{Coeff} \times \gamma_w H R$ (occurs around $0.6H$ from top).
    • Compute maximum fixed-base cantilever bending moment: $M_{base} = \text{Coeff} \times \gamma_w H^3$ (acting on vertical strip at base).
  • Step 3: Hoop Reinforcement Design & Crack Control:
    • Circumferential hoop steel: $A_{st, hoop} = \frac{T_{max}}{\sigma_{st}}$ (placed as horizontal rings on both outer and inner faces).
    • Check composite tensile stress in uncracked concrete: $\sigma_{ct} = \frac{T_{max}}{1000 t + (m - 1) A_{st}} \le \sigma_{ct, allowable}$.
  • Step 4: Vertical Cantilever Reinforcement & Base Raft Connection:
    • Vertical steel at base: $A_{st, vert} = \frac{M_{base}}{\sigma_{st} \cdot j \cdot d}$ placed on water face with full development length into the base raft.
    • Provide nominal base shear dowels and PVC water stop along the construction joint.
Eg In contrast to a sliding flexible base where hoop tension is 100% triangular ($\gamma_w H R$) at base, a fixed base reduces base hoop tension to zero while inducing high negative base bending moment.

topic: Circular Water Tank with Sliding Base (LSM Crack Width Limit)
question: Design a 320 m^3 cylindrical water tank (H=4 m) on ground with a sliding base and open top using limit state method. Limit crack width to 0.1 mm. Draw R/F details also. Use M30 concrete and Fe500 steel.
solution:
1. Tank Dimensions & Hydraulic Parameters:
  • Capacity $V = 320\text{ m}^3$; Water Depth $H = 4.0\text{ m}$; Freeboard $FB = 0.3\text{ m}$; Total Height $H_t = 4.3\text{ m}$
  • Plan Diameter: $$\frac{\pi}{4} D^2 \times 4.0 = 320 \implies D = \sqrt{\frac{320}{\pi}} = 10.09\text{ m} \approx 10.0\text{ m}$$
  • Radius: $R = 5.0\text{ m}$.
  • Materials: M30 grade concrete ($f_{ck} = 30\text{ N/mm}^2, f_{ctm} = 2.8\text{ N/mm}^2$) and Fe 500 steel ($f_y = 500\text{ N/mm}^2$). Design crack width limit $w_{max} \le 0.1\text{ mm}$ for severe exposure / liquid retention.
2. Maximum Hoop Tension (Sliding Base):
  • Because the base is flexible/sliding (movement allowed on asphalt mastic layer), wall is free of vertical bending moment, and entire hydrostatic load is resisted by pure hoop tension: $$T_{max} = \gamma_w \cdot H \cdot R = 10 \times 4.0 \times 5.0 = 200\text{ kN per metre height at base}$$
  • Factored Hoop Tension (LSM, $\gamma_f = 1.5$): $$T_u = 1.5 \times 200 = 300\text{ kN/m}$$
3. Wall Thickness & Limit State Crack Width ($w \le 0.1\text{ mm}$):
  • Under IS 3370:2009 Limit State of Serviceability for direct tension, allowable stress in Fe 500 for $w_{max} \le 0.1\text{ mm}$ is $\sigma_{st} = 130\text{ N/mm}^2$.
  • Area of Hoop Steel required at bottom 1 m: $$A_{st} = \frac{T_{max}}{\sigma_{st}} = \frac{200 \times 10^3}{130} = 1538\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$
  • Provide hoop reinforcement in 2 layers (near inner and outer faces): $$\text{Per face } A_{st} = \frac{1538}{2} = 769\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 12 mm dia hoops @ 140 mm c/c on both faces ($A_{st, prov} = 2 \times 808 = 1616\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$).
  • Check Uncracked Tensile Stress in Concrete ($D_{wall}$ sizing): $$\sigma_{ct} = \frac{T_{max}}{1000 t + (m - 1) A_{st}} \le 1.5\text{ N/mm}^2$$ With modular ratio $m = \frac{280}{3 \sigma_{cbc}} = \frac{280}{30} = 9.33$: $$1000 t + 8.33 \times 1616 \ge \frac{200 \times 10^3}{1.5} = 133333 \implies t \ge 120\text{ mm}$$ Adopt practical wall thickness: $t = 180\text{ mm}$ (uniform throughout). $$\sigma_{ct} = \frac{200000}{180000 + 13461} = 1.03\text{ N/mm}^2 < 1.5\text{ N/mm}^2 \quad \text{[Safe & watertight]}$$
  • Vertical Reinforcement (Distribution & Temperature): $$\text{Minimum percentage for } t = 180\text{ mm}: p_{min} = 0.24\%$$ $$A_{st, vert} = \frac{0.24}{100} \times 1000 \times 180 = 432\text{ mm}^2/\text{m} \implies 216\text{ mm}^2/\text{m per face}$$ Provide 8 mm dia vertical distribution bars @ 200 mm c/c on both faces ($A_{st} = 251\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$ each face).
Eg Flexible base detail: Place 2 layers of tarred paper or 12 mm bitumen pad with a central 150 mm rubber water bar between base raft and cylindrical wall to permit sliding while ensuring complete watertightness.

topic: Advantages of Circular Tanks over Rectangular Tanks
question: Enumerate two advantages why circular tanks are preferred to rectangular tanks.
solution:
1. Predominant Engineering Advantages:
  • 1. Pure Ring Tension vs Bending Moment (Higher Material Efficiency): Circular tanks resist radial liquid pressure primarily by circumferential ring/hoop tension across the entire wall cross-section, eliminating large corner hogging bending moments ($M = \frac{p L^2}{12}$) that dictate thick walls in rectangular tanks. This saves 25% to 35% concrete volume.
  • 2. Minimum Perimeter per Unit Enclosed Volume (Lowest Surface Area & Cost): For a given storage capacity $V$, a circular geometry provides the minimum perimeter ($P = \pi D = 2 \sqrt{\pi A}$) compared to a rectangular geometry ($P = 4 \sqrt{A}$), drastically reducing formwork costs, joint lengths, and potential leakage paths.
Eg For a 1000 kL tank, a circular tank requires ~20% less formwork surface area and eliminates vulnerable 90° re-entrant stress-concentration corners.

topic: Intze Water Tank Bottom Ring Beam Design
question: An Intze water tank with cylindrical walls of 11 m diameter and 5 m height. The rise of top and bottom dome is 2 m and 1.6 m respectively. The vertical height of conical dome is 2 m and diameter of ring girder at the junction of conical and bottom spherical dome is 7 m. Design only bottom ring beam. Use M 25 concrete and Fe415 steel. Draw R/F details also.
solution:
1. Geometric Dimensions & Dome Angles:
  • Cylindrical Wall: Diameter $D = 11\text{ m} \implies R_1 = 5.5\text{ m}$, Height $H = 5\text{ m}$
  • Top Dome: Rise $h_1 = 2\text{ m}$; Bottom Dome: Rise $h_2 = 1.6\text{ m}$
  • Conical Dome: Top Dia $D = 11\text{ m}$, Bottom Dia $D_0 = 7\text{ m}$, Vertical Height $H_c = 2\text{ m}$
  • Slant Height of Conical Dome: $$L_c = \sqrt{H_c^2 + \left(\frac{D - D_0}{2}\right)^2} = \sqrt{2^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{8} = 2.828\text{ m}$$
  • Inclination with horizontal: $\tan\alpha = \frac{2}{2} = 1.0 \implies \alpha = 45^\circ$, $\sin\alpha = \cos\alpha = 0.7071$
  • Bottom Spherical Dome Radius $R_2$: $$R_2 = \frac{r_0^2 + h_2^2}{2 h_2} = \frac{3.5^2 + 1.6^2}{2 \times 1.6} = \frac{12.25 + 2.56}{3.2} = 4.628\text{ m}$$ $$\sin\theta_2 = \frac{3.5}{4.628} = 0.7562 \implies \theta_2 = 49.13^\circ, \cos\theta_2 = 0.6543$$
2. Loading on Bottom Ring Beam (Ring Girder $B_2$ at Junction $D_0 = 7\text{ m}$):
  • Total vertical load transferred by Conical Dome to bottom ring beam ($W_{cone}$):
    • Weight of roof dome + Top ring beam + Cylindrical wall ($11\text{ m}$ dia) + Water directly above conical frustum + Self weight of conical slab.
    • Water load above conical frustum: $$V_{water} = \frac{\pi}{3} H_c (R_1^2 + R_0^2 + R_1 R_0) - \pi R_0^2 H_c + \text{cylindrical column} \approx 620\text{ m}^3 \implies W_w = 6200\text{ kN}$$
    • Total cumulative vertical load at base of conical dome: $W_T \approx 7850\text{ kN}$.
  • Vertical load per unit circumference along $D_0 = 7\text{ m}$: $$V = \frac{W_T}{\pi D_0} = \frac{7850}{\pi \times 7} = 357.0\text{ kN/m}$$
  • Inward horizontal thrust exerted by Conical Dome: $$H_{inward} = \frac{V}{\tan\alpha} = \frac{357.0}{\tan 45^\circ} = 357.0\text{ kN/m}$$
  • Outward horizontal thrust exerted by Bottom Spherical Dome:
    • Total downward load on bottom spherical dome (water above + self-weight of dome $\approx 1250\text{ kN}$): $$V_{dome} = \frac{1250}{\pi \times 7} = 56.84\text{ kN/m}$$ $$H_{outward} = \frac{V_{dome}}{\tan\theta_2} = \frac{56.84}{\tan 49.13^\circ} = \frac{56.84}{1.155} = 49.2\text{ kN/m}$$
  • Net Inward Horizontal Force on Ring Beam: $$H_{net} = H_{inward} - H_{outward} = 357.0 - 49.2 = 307.8\text{ kN/m (Inward Radial Thrust)}$$
  • Hoop Compression in Bottom Ring Beam: $$C_{hoop} = H_{net} \times \frac{D_0}{2} = 307.8 \times 3.5 = 1077.3\text{ kN (Compression)}$$
3. Section Design & Reinforcement:
  • Allowable Direct Compressive Stress for M25 concrete: $\sigma_{cc} = 6.0\text{ N/mm}^2$
  • Required Cross-Sectional Area: $$A_c = \frac{C_{hoop}}{\sigma_{cc}} = \frac{1077.3 \times 10^3}{6.0} = 179550\text{ mm}^2$$ Adopt Beam Size: $600\text{ mm wide} \times 900\text{ mm deep}$ ($A_{prov} = 540000\text{ mm}^2 \gg 179550\text{ mm}^2$ to also carry circumferential circular girder bending moments across columns).
  • Nominal & Continuity Steel ($0.8\%$ of $A_c$ for column frame action): $$A_{st} = \frac{0.8}{100} \times 600 \times 900 = 4320\text{ mm}^2$$ Provide 8 nos. 25 mm dia bars (4 at top, 4 at bottom) ($A_{st, prov} = 3927\text{ mm}^2$) plus 4 nos. 16 mm side-face bars. Eg The Intze tank's signature structural innovation is this conical-to-spherical junction: the heavy inward thrust of the conical wall counteracts the outward thrust of the bottom dome, minimizing hoop stresses on the ring beam.

topic: Components of Overhead Tank Staging System
question: Enlist the components of the staging system of an overhead tank.
solution:
1. Essential Structural Components of Elevated Staging:
  • 1. Supporting Columns (Shaft / Space Frame Columns): Circular, octagonal, or square RCC columns arranged symmetrically on a pitch circle to transfer vertical gravity loads and lateral shears to foundations.
  • 2. Horizontal Ring Bracings: Continuous circumferential beams spaced at 3 m to 4.5 m vertical intervals to reduce column effective slenderness ($l_{eff}$) and resist frame sway under wind/seismic forces.
  • 3. Top Ring Girder / Cap Beam: Heavy circular girder resting directly on column heads that supports the tank container and ensures uniform distribution of superstructure loads.
  • 4. Foundation System (Raft / Annular Strip / Piles): Annular circular raft, solid circular plate, or pile caps with tie beams that transfer column axial loads and overturning moments into the bearing stratum.
Eg For staging heights > 15 m, an RC continuous hollow cylindrical shaft is preferred over columns due to superior torsional rigidity and rapid slip-form construction.

topic: Hoop Reinforcement Design for Overhead Cylindrical Tank
question: Design the hoop reinforcement for a cylindrical overhead tank of diameter 8 m and water depth 5 m. The tank is open at top and supported on staging. Compute maximum hoop tension. Also sketch Wall section showing hoop bars, vertical bars, cover, and spacing.
solution:
1. Given Data:
  • Diameter $D = 8.0\text{ m} \implies R = 4.0\text{ m}$; Water Depth $H = 5.0\text{ m}$; Freeboard $FB = 0.3\text{ m}$
  • Materials: M25 concrete ($\sigma_{ct} = 1.3\text{ N/mm}^2, \sigma_{cbc} = 8.5\text{ N/mm}^2$) and Fe 415 steel ($\sigma_{st} = 130\text{ N/mm}^2$ per IS 3370:2009 for liquid retaining faces)
  • Unit weight of water: $\gamma_w = 10\text{ kN/m}^3$
2. Maximum Hoop Tension & Steel Calculation:
  • Maximum hydrostatic water pressure at base: $$p_{max} = \gamma_w \cdot H = 10 \times 5.0 = 50\text{ kN/m}^2$$
  • Maximum Hoop Tension at base: $$T_{max} = p_{max} \cdot R = 50 \times 4.0 = 200\text{ kN per metre height}$$
  • Area of Hoop Reinforcement Required at Base: $$A_{st, hoop} = \frac{T_{max}}{\sigma_{st}} = \frac{200 \times 10^3}{130} = 1538.5\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$
  • Arrangement in 2 rings (water face and outer face): $$A_{st}\text{ per face} = \frac{1538.5}{2} = 769.25\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 16 mm dia hoop bars @ 130 mm c/c on both faces ($A_{st, prov} = 2 \times 1546 = 3092\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$).
3. Concrete Thickness Sizing (Uncracked Concrete Stress Check):
  • Direct Tensile Stress in uncracked composite section ($m = 11$): $$\sigma_{ct} = \frac{T_{max}}{1000 t + (m - 1) A_{st}} \le \sigma_{ct, perm} = 1.3\text{ N/mm}^2$$ $$1000 t + 10 \times 3092 \ge \frac{200 \times 10^3}{1.3} = 153846 \implies 1000 t \ge 122926 \implies t \ge 123\text{ mm}$$ Adopt practical wall thickness: $t = 200\text{ mm}$ (ensures minimum cover and ease of casting). $$\sigma_{ct} = \frac{200000}{200000 + 30920} = 0.866\text{ N/mm}^2 < 1.3\text{ N/mm}^2 \quad \text{[Extremely Safe]}$$
  • Vertical Reinforcement (Temperature & Shrinkage): $$p_{min} = 0.24\% \implies A_{st, vert} = \frac{0.24}{100} \times 1000 \times 200 = 480\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 10 mm dia vertical bars @ 160 mm c/c on both faces ($A_{st} = 2 \times 491 = 982\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$).
  • Clear Cover: $35\text{ mm}$ clear cover to outer hoops on liquid face.
Eg Detailing requirement: Lap splices in circular hoop rings must be staggered by at least 1.5 m circumferentially, with minimum lap length of $50 \phi = 800\text{ mm}$ per IS 3370.

topic: Cylindrical Silo Design using Janssen's Theory
question: A silo with internal diameter 4.5 m, height of cylindrical portion 16 m and central opening with 0.5 m is to be built to store wheat. Design only the cylindrical portion of the silo using M25 grade concrete and Fe-415 steel. Given: Pressure ratio, K = 0.5 while filling, Unit weight of wheat = 8.5 kN/m^3, Angle of wall friction = 0.75 phi while filling & = 0.60 phi while emptying. Use Janssen's theory for pressure calculations., Refer Table 1
solution:
1. Silo Geometric & Material Parameters:
  • Internal Diameter $D = 4.5\text{ m} \implies \text{Radius } R_s = 2.25\text{ m}$; Height of cylindrical portion $H = 16\text{ m}$
  • Central discharge opening dia $d_0 = 0.5\text{ m}$
  • Stored Material (Wheat): Unit weight $\gamma = 8.5\text{ kN/m}^3$; Angle of internal friction $\phi \approx 28^\circ$ ($\tan\phi = 0.5317$)
  • Pressure ratio $K = 0.5$ (filling); Coefficient of wall friction:
    • Filling: $\mu' = \tan(0.75 \times 28^\circ) = \tan 21^\circ = 0.3839$
    • Emptying: $\mu' = \tan(0.60 \times 28^\circ) = \tan 16.8^\circ = 0.3019$ (Emptying case yields lower friction, hence larger lateral pressures; govern design!)
  • Hydraulic Radius $R$: $$R = \frac{\text{Cross-sectional Area}}{\text{Perimeter}} = \frac{\frac{\pi}{4} D^2}{\pi D} = \frac{D}{4} = \frac{4.5}{4} = 1.125\text{ m}$$
2. Janssen's Lateral Pressure Computation ($h = 16\text{ m}$):
  • Janssen's Horizontal Pressure Formula: $$p_h = \frac{\gamma R}{\mu'} \left[ 1 - e^{-\frac{\mu' K h}{R}} \right]$$
  • Exponent Factor at bottom of cylinder ($h = 16\text{ m}$, using emptying values $K=0.5, \mu'=0.3019$): $$z = \frac{\mu' K h}{R} = \frac{0.3019 \times 0.5 \times 16}{1.125} = \frac{2.4152}{1.125} = 2.1468$$ $$1 - e^{-z} = 1 - e^{-2.1468} = 1 - 0.1169 = 0.8831$$
  • Asymptotic maximum pressure: $$\frac{\gamma R}{\mu'} = \frac{8.5 \times 1.125}{0.3019} = \frac{9.5625}{0.3019} = 31.67\text{ kN/m}^2$$
  • Maximum Horizontal Pressure at Base: $$p_h = 31.67 \times 0.8831 = 27.97\text{ kN/m}^2$$
  • Per IS 4995 (Part I), apply an overpressure factor of $1.35$ for dynamic discharge: $$p_{h, des} = 1.35 \times 27.97 = 37.76\text{ kN/m}^2$$
3. Hoop Reinforcement & Wall Thickness:
  • Maximum Hoop Tension at bottom of cylinder per metre height: $$T = p_{h, des} \cdot \frac{D}{2} = 37.76 \times 2.25 = 84.96\text{ kN/m}$$
  • Hoop Steel Required ($f_y = 415\text{ N/mm}^2, \sigma_{st} = 130\text{ N/mm}^2$): $$A_{st, hoop} = \frac{T}{\sigma_{st}} = \frac{84.96 \times 10^3}{130} = 653.5\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 12 mm dia hoops @ 160 mm c/c ($A_{st, prov} = 707\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$) arranged in two curtains (near inner and outer faces).
  • Wall Thickness Check: $$\sigma_{ct} = \frac{T}{1000 t + (m - 1) A_{st}} \le 1.3\text{ N/mm}^2 \implies t \ge \frac{84960}{1.3 \times 1000} \approx 65\text{ mm}$$ Adopt minimum construction thickness per IS 4995: $t = 160\text{ mm}$.
  • Vertical Reinforcement (Compressive load due to grain wall friction):
    • Vertical friction load on wall: $W_{friction} = \gamma A h - p_v A$.
    • Provide minimum vertical reinforcement $0.3\% = \frac{0.3}{100} \times 1000 \times 160 = 480\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$.
    • Provide 10 mm dia vertical bars @ 160 mm c/c ($A_{st} = 491\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$) on both faces.
Eg Silo grain pressures do not increase linearly like hydrostatic pressure; beyond a transition depth of $2D$, lateral pressure approaches an asymptote governed by wall friction.

topic: Square Bunker Hopper Bottom Design
question: Design the hopper bottom of the square bunker shown in Fig. 1, to store coal of density 8 kN/m^3 and angle of repose phi = 25 deg.
solution:
1. Geometric Proportions & Loading (From Fig. 1):
  • Bunker Plan: Square $a \times a = 3.5\text{ m} \times 3.5\text{ m}$; Discharge opening $0.5\text{ m} \times 0.5\text{ m}$
  • Vertical Wall Height $H_v = 3.5\text{ m}$; Hopper Depth $h_h = 2.0\text{ m}$; Surcharge cone rise = $0.7\text{ m}$
  • Stored Material (Coal): Density $\gamma = 8.0\text{ kN/m}^3$, Angle of internal friction $\phi = 25^\circ$
  • Hopper Wall Slope: $\tan\theta = \frac{h_h}{(a - d_0)/2} = \frac{2.0}{1.5} = 1.333 \implies \theta = 53.13^\circ$, $\sin\theta = 0.80, \cos\theta = 0.60$
  • Rankine Coefficient of Active Earth Pressure: $$K_a = \frac{1 - \sin 25^\circ}{1 + \sin 25^\circ} = \frac{1 - 0.4226}{1 + 0.4226} = 0.406$$
2. Load on Sloping Hopper Bottom:
  • Total weight of coal carried by hopper bottom ($W_t$):
    • Volume of vertical portion + surcharge cone: $V_1 = 3.5^2 \times 3.5 + \frac{1}{3} \times 3.5^2 \times 0.7 = 42.875 + 2.858 = 45.73\text{ m}^3$
    • Volume of inverted frustum of hopper: $V_2 = \frac{2.0}{3} [3.5^2 + 0.5^2 + 3.5 \times 0.5] = \frac{2}{3} [12.25 + 0.25 + 1.75] = 9.50\text{ m}^3$
    • Total Weight of Coal: $W_{coal} = \gamma (V_1 + V_2) = 8.0 \times (45.73 + 9.50) = 441.8\text{ kN}$
    • Self-weight of hopper slab ($t = 160\text{ mm}$): $W_{slab} \approx 65\text{ kN} \implies W_{total} = 506.8\text{ kN}$.
  • Direct Tension along Sloping Face (Meridional Tension per metre width at top edge): $$T_m = \frac{W_{total}}{4 \times a \times \sin\theta} = \frac{506.8}{4 \times 3.5 \times 0.80} = 45.25\text{ kN/m}$$
  • Normal Pressure on Sloping Plate at Junction: $$p_n = p_v \cos^2\theta + p_h \sin^2\theta$$ With vertical pressure $p_v = \gamma \times H = 8.0 \times 4.2 = 33.6\text{ kN/m}^2$: $$p_h = K_a p_v = 0.406 \times 33.6 = 13.64\text{ kN/m}^2$$ $$p_n = (33.6 \times 0.36) + (13.64 \times 0.64) = 12.10 + 8.73 = 20.83\text{ kN/m}^2$$
  • Bending Moment in Sloping Slab (spanning horizontally between hip girders with effective span $L_{eff} \approx 3.0\text{ m}$): $$M = \frac{p_n L_{eff}^2}{10} = \frac{20.83 \times 3.0^2}{10} = 18.75\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m/m}$$
3. Reinforcement Details:
  • Hopper Slab Thickness: $t = 160\text{ mm}$ ($d = 130\text{ mm}$).
  • Steel for Combined Bending + Direct Tension ($f_y = 415\text{ N/mm}^2, \sigma_{st} = 130\text{ N/mm}^2$): $$A_{st, horizontal} = \frac{M}{\sigma_{st} \cdot j \cdot d} = \frac{18.75 \times 10^6}{130 \times 0.85 \times 130} = 1305\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 16 mm dia bars @ 150 mm c/c ($A_{st} = 1340\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$) running horizontally.
  • Sloping Steel (Meridional direction): $$A_{st, meridional} = \frac{T_m}{\sigma_{st}} = \frac{45.25 \times 10^3}{130} = 348\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Governed by temperature & bending distribution steel ($0.3\%$): $$A_{st, prov} = \frac{0.3}{100} \times 1000 \times 160 = 480\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 10 mm dia bars @ 160 mm c/c ($A_{st} = 491\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$) along the slope.
Eg Sloping hopper slabs must have a minimum inclination angle $\theta \ge \phi + 15^\circ$ to guarantee free gravity discharge without funneling or bridging.
formatted_solution:
1. Geometric Proportions & Loading (From Fig. 1):
  • Bunker Plan: Square $a \times a = 3.5\text{ m} \times 3.5\text{ m}$; Discharge opening $0.5\text{ m} \times 0.5\text{ m}$
  • Vertical Wall Height $H_v = 3.5\text{ m}$; Hopper Depth $h_h = 2.0\text{ m}$; Surcharge cone rise = $0.7\text{ m}$
  • Stored Material (Coal): Density $\gamma = 8.0\text{ kN/m}^3$, Angle of internal friction $\phi = 25^\circ$
  • Hopper Wall Slope: $\tan\theta = \frac{h_h}{(a - d_0)/2} = \frac{2.0}{1.5} = 1.333 \implies \theta = 53.13^\circ$, $\sin\theta = 0.80, \cos\theta = 0.60$
  • Rankine Coefficient of Active Earth Pressure: $$K_a = \frac{1 - \sin 25^\circ}{1 + \sin 25^\circ} = \frac{1 - 0.4226}{1 + 0.4226} = 0.406$$
2. Load on Sloping Hopper Bottom:
  • Total weight of coal carried by hopper bottom ($W_t$):
    • Volume of vertical portion + surcharge cone: $V_1 = 3.5^2 \times 3.5 + \frac{1}{3} \times 3.5^2 \times 0.7 = 42.875 + 2.858 = 45.73\text{ m}^3$
    • Volume of inverted frustum of hopper: $V_2 = \frac{2.0}{3} [3.5^2 + 0.5^2 + 3.5 \times 0.5] = \frac{2}{3} [12.25 + 0.25 + 1.75] = 9.50\text{ m}^3$
    • Total Weight of Coal: $W_{coal} = \gamma (V_1 + V_2) = 8.0 \times (45.73 + 9.50) = 441.8\text{ kN}$
    • Self-weight of hopper slab ($t = 160\text{ mm}$): $W_{slab} \approx 65\text{ kN} \implies W_{total} = 506.8\text{ kN}$.
  • Direct Tension along Sloping Face (Meridional Tension per metre width at top edge): $$T_m = \frac{W_{total}}{4 \times a \times \sin\theta} = \frac{506.8}{4 \times 3.5 \times 0.80} = 45.25\text{ kN/m}$$
  • Normal Pressure on Sloping Plate at Junction: $$p_n = p_v \cos^2\theta + p_h \sin^2\theta$$ With vertical pressure $p_v = \gamma \times H = 8.0 \times 4.2 = 33.6\text{ kN/m}^2$: $$p_h = K_a p_v = 0.406 \times 33.6 = 13.64\text{ kN/m}^2$$ $$p_n = (33.6 \times 0.36) + (13.64 \times 0.64) = 12.10 + 8.73 = 20.83\text{ kN/m}^2$$
  • Bending Moment in Sloping Slab (spanning horizontally between hip girders with effective span $L_{eff} \approx 3.0\text{ m}$): $$M = \frac{p_n L_{eff}^2}{10} = \frac{20.83 \times 3.0^2}{10} = 18.75\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m/m}$$
3. Reinforcement Details:
  • Hopper Slab Thickness: $t = 160\text{ mm}$ ($d = 130\text{ mm}$).
  • Steel for Combined Bending + Direct Tension ($f_y = 415\text{ N/mm}^2, \sigma_{st} = 130\text{ N/mm}^2$): $$A_{st, horizontal} = \frac{M}{\sigma_{st} \cdot j \cdot d} = \frac{18.75 \times 10^6}{130 \times 0.85 \times 130} = 1305\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 16 mm dia bars @ 150 mm c/c ($A_{st} = 1340\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$) running horizontally.
  • Sloping Steel (Meridional direction): $$A_{st, meridional} = \frac{T_m}{\sigma_{st}} = \frac{45.25 \times 10^3}{130} = 348\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Governed by temperature & bending distribution steel ($0.3\%$): $$A_{st, prov} = \frac{0.3}{100} \times 1000 \times 160 = 480\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 10 mm dia bars @ 160 mm c/c ($A_{st} = 491\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$) along the slope.
Eg Sloping hopper slabs must have a minimum inclination angle $\theta \ge \phi + 15^\circ$ to guarantee free gravity discharge without funneling or bridging.

topic: RC Grid Floor Design by Rankine-Grashoff Method
question: Design a reinforced concrete grid floor to cover a floor area of 12 m X 16 m. The spacing of the ribs in the both directions is 2.0 m. Design the rib carrying maximum bending moment? Take LL= 4.2 kN/m^2. Draw R/F details also.
solution:
1. Dimensions & Load Partition (Rankine-Grashoff Method):
  • Overall Hall Dimensions: $L_x = 12\text{ m}$ (short span), $L_y = 16\text{ m}$ (long span)
  • Rib spacing in both directions: $s_x = s_y = 2.0\text{ m}$
  • Number of ribs: Along X-direction $= \frac{16}{2} - 1 = 7\text{ ribs}$; Along Y-direction $= \frac{12}{2} - 1 = 5\text{ ribs}$
  • Thickness of topping slab: $t_s = 100\text{ mm}$
  • Trial size of rib beams: Width $b_w = 200\text{ mm}$, Depth $D = 750\text{ mm}$ ($d = 700\text{ mm}$)
  • Loads per square metre:
    • Slab self-weight: $0.10 \times 25 = 2.5\text{ kN/m}^2$
    • Rib self-weight: $(0.75 - 0.10) \times 0.20 \times 25 \times \frac{2 + 2}{2 \times 2} = 3.25\text{ kN/m}^2$
    • Floor finish: $1.0\text{ kN/m}^2$; Live Load: $LL = 4.2\text{ kN/m}^2$
    • Total Characteristic Load: $q = 2.5 + 3.25 + 1.0 + 4.2 = 10.95\text{ kN/m}^2$
    • Factored Load: $q_u = 1.5 \times 10.95 = 16.425\text{ kN/m}^2$
2. Load Sharing Between Ribs (Plate/Grid Deflection Equivalence):
  • Load transferred to short ribs ($q_{ux}$) and long ribs ($q_{uy}$): $$q_{ux} = q_u \left( \frac{L_y^4}{L_x^4 + L_y^4} \right) = 16.425 \times \left( \frac{16^4}{12^4 + 16^4} \right) = 16.425 \times \frac{65536}{20736 + 65536} = 16.425 \times 0.7596 = 12.48\text{ kN/m}^2$$ $$q_{uy} = q_u - q_{ux} = 16.425 - 12.48 = 3.945\text{ kN/m}^2$$
  • Load per metre run on central short-span rib (spacing $s = 2.0\text{ m}$): $$w_{ux} = q_{ux} \times s = 12.48 \times 2.0 = 24.96\text{ kN/m}$$
3. Maximum Bending Moment & Shear in Critical Short Rib:
  • Short-span rib carries maximum bending moment (span $L_x = 12\text{ m}$): $$M_{ux} = \frac{w_{ux} L_x^2}{8} = \frac{24.96 \times 12^2}{8} = 449.28\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Maximum Factored Shear Force at Support: $$V_{ux} = \frac{w_{ux} L_x}{2} = \frac{24.96 \times 12}{2} = 149.76\text{ kN}$$
4. Reinforcement Design (T-Beam Action):
  • Flange width $b_f = s = 2000\text{ mm}$ or $L_0/6 + b_w + 6 D_f = 2000 + 200 + 600 = 2800\text{ mm} \implies b_f = 2000\text{ mm}$
  • Moment capacity of flange ($D_f = 100\text{ mm}$): $$M_{u, flange} = 0.36 f_{ck} b_f D_f (d - 0.42 D_f) = 0.36 \times 25 \times 2000 \times 100 \times (700 - 42) \times 10^{-6} = 1184.4\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m} > 449.28\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$ Neutral axis lies inside flange ($x_u < D_f$).
  • Tensile Steel Area ($f_y = 500\text{ N/mm}^2, d = 700\text{ mm}$): $$A_{st} = \frac{0.5 \times 25}{500} \left[ 1 - \sqrt{1 - \frac{4.59 \times 449.28 \times 10^6}{25 \times 2000 \times 700^2}} \right] \times 2000 \times 700 = 1532\text{ mm}^2$$ Provide 5 nos. 20 mm dia bars ($A_{st, prov} = 1570\text{ mm}^2$) in the tension zone.
  • Shear Reinforcement: $$\tau_v = \frac{V_{ux}}{b_w d} = \frac{149.76 \times 10^3}{200 \times 700} = 1.07\text{ N/mm}^2 > \tau_c = 0.62\text{ N/mm}^2$$ Provide 8 mm dia 2-legged stirrups @ 140 mm c/c near supports, increasing to 250 mm c/c at mid-span.
Eg Grid floors provide large column-free spaces (12 m to 20 m) with architecturally aesthetic exposed coffered soffits, where intersecting ribs act interactively to redistribute peak concentrated loads.

topic: Rankine-Grashoff Method for Grid Structures
question: Discuss in brief about Rankine-Grashoff method of analysis and design of Grid Structures.
solution:
1. Governing Assumptions & Formulation:
  • 1. Deflection Compatibility at Intersections: Assumes the central intersecting ribs in the mutually perpendicular directions ($X$ and $Y$) undergo identical central deflection ($\delta_x = \delta_y$).
  • 2. Fourth-Power Load Partitioning: Since central deflection for a simply supported beam is $\delta = \frac{5 w L^4}{384 E I}$, equating deflections yields the classic inverse-fourth-power load division: $$q_x = q \cdot \frac{L_y^4}{L_x^4 + L_y^4}, \quad q_y = q \cdot \frac{L_x^4}{L_x^4 + L_y^4}$$ The stiffer shorter span carries the predominant fraction ($L_y^4 / (L_x^4 + L_y^4)$) of the total gravity load.
  • 3. Limitation: Ignores torsional stiffness ($G J$) of intersecting ribs and assumes simply supported boundary conditions, making it an approximate but conservative design tool.
Eg For an aspect ratio of $L_y / L_x = 1.33$, Rankine-Grashoff allocates ~76% of the load to the short-span ribs and only 24% to the long-span ribs.

topic: Rigorous Analysis of Grid Floors (Plate Theory)
question: List out the mathematical expressions for calculation of moments, shear, and torsion using method of Rigorous Analysis.
solution:
1. Plate-Theory Governing Equations for Orthotropic Grids:
  • 1. Governing Fourth-Order Differential Equation: $$D_x \frac{\partial^4 w}{\partial x^4} + 2 H \frac{\partial^4 w}{\partial x^2 \partial y^2} + D_y \frac{\partial^4 w}{\partial y^4} = q(x, y)$$ where $D_x = \frac{E I_x}{s_y}, D_y = \frac{E I_y}{s_x}$ are flexural rigidities per unit width, and $2H = \frac{G J_x}{s_y} + \frac{G J_y}{s_x}$ is the torsional coupling rigidity.
  • 2. Bending Moments in Ribs: $$M_x = -D_x \frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial x^2}, \quad M_y = -D_y \frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial y^2}$$
  • 3. Torsional Moments in Ribs: $$M_{xy} = C_x \frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial x \partial y}, \quad M_{yx} = -C_y \frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial x \partial y}$$
  • 4. Vertical Shear Forces: $$Q_x = -\frac{\partial M_x}{\partial x} - \frac{\partial M_{yx}}{\partial y}, \quad Q_y = -\frac{\partial M_y}{\partial y} + \frac{\partial M_{xy}}{\partial x}$$
Eg Rigorous orthotropic plate analysis reduces calculated mid-span bending moments by 15% to 20% compared to Rankine-Grashoff by explicitly accounting for torsional load shedding between adjacent ribs.

topic: Flat Slab Interior Panel Design (Direct Design Method)
question: An area of size 15m X 15m is to be covered by Flat slab with column spaced at 5 m in each direction. Design interior panel. Take LL= 4 kN/m^2. Assume appropriate dimensions for the drop panel and column head and incorporate them in the design. Draw R/F details also.
solution:
1. Geometric Dimensions & Preliminary Proportions (IS 456 Clause 31):
  • Floor Area: $15\text{ m} \times 15\text{ m}$ with 3 panels of $L_1 = L_2 = 5.0\text{ m}$ in each direction.
  • Column Dimensions: Column head diameter $D_c = \frac{L}{4} = \frac{5.0}{4} = 1.25\text{ m}$. Circular column dia $D_{col} = 500\text{ mm}$.
  • Drop Dimensions: Minimum length $\ge \frac{L}{3} = \frac{5.0}{3} = 1.67\text{ m}$. Adopt square drop: $2.5\text{ m} \times 2.5\text{ m}$ ($L/2$).
  • Slab Thickness ($t_s$): Based on deflection criteria ($L/32$ for drops): $$t_s = \frac{5000}{32} \approx 156\text{ mm} \implies \text{Adopt slab thickness } t_s = 180\text{ mm}$$
  • Drop Thickness ($t_d$): Drop depth $\ge t_s / 4 = 45\text{ mm}$. Adopt total depth through drop: $D_{drop} = 250\text{ mm}$ (drop projection = $70\text{ mm}$).
  • Design Loads:
    • Slab self-weight: $0.18 \times 25 = 4.5\text{ kN/m}^2$
    • Floor finish: $1.0\text{ kN/m}^2$; Live Load: $LL = 4.0\text{ kN/m}^2$
    • Total Design Factored Load: $w_u = 1.5 \times (4.5 + 1.0 + 4.0) = 1.5 \times 9.5 = 14.25\text{ kN/m}^2$.
2. Total Design Static Moment ($M_0$):
  • Clear Span ($L_n$): $$L_n = L_1 - D_c = 5.0 - 1.25 = 3.75\text{ m} \ge 0.65 L_1 = 3.25\text{ m} \quad \text{[OK]}$$
  • Total Design Moment per Panel (IS 456 Cl. 31.4.2.2): $$W = w_u \times L_2 \times L_n = 14.25 \times 5.0 \times 3.75 = 267.19\text{ kN}$$ $$M_0 = \frac{W L_n}{8} = \frac{267.19 \times 3.75}{8} = 125.25\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Moment Apportionment for Interior Panel (IS 456 Table 28):
    • Total Negative Design Moment: $M_{u,-} = 0.65 M_0 = 0.65 \times 125.25 = 81.41\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$
    • Total Positive Design Moment: $M_{u,+} = 0.35 M_0 = 0.35 \times 125.25 = 43.84\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$
3. Strip Moment Distribution & Steel Calculations:
  • Strip Widths: Column Strip width $= 0.5 L_2 = 2.5\text{ m}$; Middle Strip width $= 2.5\text{ m}$.
  • Column Strip Moments:
    • Negative Moment ($75\%$ of $M_{u,-}$): $M_{cs,-} = 0.75 \times 81.41 = 61.06\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$ (resisted by $D_{drop} = 250\text{ mm}, d = 215\text{ mm}$).
    • Positive Moment ($60\%$ of $M_{u,+}$): $M_{cs,+} = 0.60 \times 43.84 = 26.30\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$ (resisted by $t_s = 180\text{ mm}, d = 150\text{ mm}$).
  • Middle Strip Moments:
    • Negative Moment ($25\%$ of $M_{u,-}$): $M_{ms,-} = 0.25 \times 81.41 = 20.35\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$ ($d = 150\text{ mm}$).
    • Positive Moment ($40\%$ of $M_{u,+}$): $M_{ms,+} = 0.40 \times 43.84 = 17.54\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$ ($d = 150\text{ mm}$).
  • Reinforcement Details ($f_y = 500\text{ N/mm}^2$):
    • Column Strip Negative Steel: $A_{st} = \frac{61.06 \times 10^6}{0.87 \times 500 \times 0.9 \times 215} = 725\text{ mm}^2$ across $2.5\text{ m} \implies$ Provide 10 mm dia bars @ 180 mm c/c ($A_{st} = 436\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$).
    • Column Strip Positive Steel: $A_{st} = 450\text{ mm}^2$ across $2.5\text{ m} \implies$ Provide 10 mm dia bars @ 220 mm c/c.
    • Middle Strip Steel (Top & Bottom): Provide 10 mm dia bars @ 250 mm c/c throughout.
4. Two-Way Punching Shear Check at Column Head:
  • Critical perimeter at $d/2 = 215 / 2 = 107.5\text{ mm}$ from column head: $$D_{crit} = D_c + d = 1250 + 215 = 1465\text{ mm} \implies b_0 = \pi \times 1465 = 4602\text{ mm}$$
  • Factored Punching Shear Force: $$V_u = w_u (L_1 L_2 - \frac{\pi}{4} D_{crit}^2) = 14.25 (25 - 1.68) = 332.3\text{ kN}$$
  • Punching Shear Stress: $$\tau_v = \frac{V_u}{b_0 d} = \frac{332.3 \times 10^3}{4602 \times 215} = 0.336\text{ N/mm}^2$$
  • Permissible Shear Stress (IS 456 Cl. 31.6.3.1): $$k_s = 1.0, \quad \tau_c = 0.25 \sqrt{f_{ck}} = 0.25 \sqrt{25} = 1.25\text{ N/mm}^2$$ $$\tau_v = 0.336\text{ N/mm}^2 \ll 1.25\text{ N/mm}^2 \quad \text{[Safe in Punching Shear without shear reinforcement]}$$
Eg Drops thicken the slab precisely where negative hogging moments and two-way punching shears peak, preserving thin spans between columns.

    • Positive Moment ($60\%$ of $M_{u,+}$): $M_{cs,+} = 0.60 \times 43.84 = 26.30\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$ (resisted by $t_s = 180\text{ mm}, d = 150\text{ mm}$).
  • Middle Strip Moments:
    • Negative Moment ($25\%$ of $M_{u,-}$): $M_{ms,-} = 0.25 \times 81.41 = 20.35\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$ ($d = 150\text{ mm}$).
    • Positive Moment ($40\%$ of $M_{u,+}$): $M_{ms,+} = 0.40 \times 43.84 = 17.54\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$ ($d = 150\text{ mm}$).
  • Reinforcement Details ($f_y = 500\text{ N/mm}^2$):
    • Column Strip Negative Steel: $A_{st} = \frac{61.06 \times 10^6}{0.87 \times 500 \times 0.9 \times 215} = 725\text{ mm}^2$ across $2.5\text{ m} \implies$ Provide 10 mm dia bars @ 180 mm c/c ($A_{st} = 436\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$).
    • Column Strip Positive Steel: $A_{st} = 450\text{ mm}^2$ across $2.5\text{ m} \implies$ Provide 10 mm dia bars @ 220 mm c/c.
    • Middle Strip Steel (Top & Bottom): Provide 10 mm dia bars @ 250 mm c/c throughout.
4. Two-Way Punching Shear Check at Column Head:
  • Critical perimeter at $d/2 = 215 / 2 = 107.5\text{ mm}$ from column head: $$D_{crit} = D_c + d = 1250 + 215 = 1465\text{ mm} \implies b_0 = \pi \times 1465 = 4602\text{ mm}$$
  • Factored Punching Shear Force: $$V_u = w_u (L_1 L_2 - \frac{\pi}{4} D_{crit}^2) = 14.25 (25 - 1.68) = 332.3\text{ kN}$$
  • Punching Shear Stress: $$\tau_v = \frac{V_u}{b_0 d} = \frac{332.3 \times 10^3}{4602 \times 215} = 0.336\text{ N/mm}^2$$
  • Permissible Shear Stress (IS 456 Cl. 31.6.3.1): $$k_s = 1.0, \quad \tau_c = 0.25 \sqrt{f_{ck}} = 0.25 \sqrt{25} = 1.25\text{ N/mm}^2$$ $$\tau_v = 0.336\text{ N/mm}^2 \ll 1.25\text{ N/mm}^2 \quad \text{[Safe in Punching Shear without shear reinforcement]}$$
Eg Drops thicken the slab precisely where negative hogging moments and two-way punching shears peak, preserving thin spans between columns.

topic: Flat Slab Exterior Panel Design
question: Design the exterior panel of a flat slab with panel size 6.5 m x 6.5 m. The slab thickness is 300 mm and the drop panel is 3 m x 3 m with a thickness of 450 mm. The building is braced. Column diameter = 700 mm and column head diameter = 1000 mm. Live load = 7.5 kN/m^2. Assume M20 concrete and Fe500 steel. Sketch the reinforcement details for the column strip and middle strip.
solution:
1. Panel Parameters & Load Formulation:
  • Panel Dimensions: $L_1 = L_2 = 6.5\text{ m}$; Slab thickness $t_s = 300\text{ mm}$; Drop $3.0\text{ m} \times 3.0\text{ m} \times 450\text{ mm}$
  • Column dia $D_{col} = 700\text{ mm}$, Column head dia $D_c = 1000\text{ mm}$ ($1.0\text{ m}$)
  • Materials: M20 concrete ($f_{ck} = 20\text{ N/mm}^2$) and Fe 500 steel ($f_y = 500\text{ N/mm}^2$)
  • Design Loads:
    • Slab self-weight: $0.30 \times 25 = 7.5\text{ kN/m}^2$
    • Drop excess weight averaged over panel: $\frac{(0.45 - 0.30) \times 25 \times 9}{6.5^2} = 0.80\text{ kN/m}^2$
    • Floor finish: $1.2\text{ kN/m}^2$; Live Load: $7.5\text{ kN/m}^2$
    • Total Factored Load: $w_u = 1.5 \times (7.5 + 0.80 + 1.2 + 7.5) = 1.5 \times 17.0 = 25.5\text{ kN/m}^2$.
2. Design Moment $M_0$ & End-Span Distribution:
  • Clear Span $L_n = L_1 - D_c = 6.5 - 1.0 = 5.5\text{ m} \ge 0.65 L_1 = 4.225\text{ m}$
  • Total Design Moment (IS 456 Cl. 31.4.2.2): $$W = w_u \times L_2 \times L_n = 25.5 \times 6.5 \times 5.5 = 911.6\text{ kN}$$ $$M_0 = \frac{W L_n}{8} = \frac{911.6 \times 5.5}{8} = 626.7\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Moment Distribution for Exterior Panel with Braced/Monolithic Column (IS 456 Table 28):
    • Exterior Negative Moment: $M_{u, ext,-} = 0.26 M_0 = 0.26 \times 626.7 = 162.9\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$
    • Positive (Span) Moment: $M_{u,+} = 0.52 M_0 = 0.52 \times 626.7 = 325.9\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$
    • Interior Negative Moment: $M_{u, int,-} = 0.70 M_0 = 0.70 \times 626.7 = 438.7\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$
3. Strip Allotment & Reinforcement:
  • Width of Column Strip $= 0.5 L_2 = 3.25\text{ m}$; Middle Strip $= 3.25\text{ m}$.
  • Effective depths: In drop $d = 450 - 35 = 415\text{ mm}$; In slab $d = 300 - 30 = 270\text{ mm}$.
  • Column Strip Interior Negative ($75\%$ of $438.7 = 329.0\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$ at drop): $$A_{st} = \frac{329.0 \times 10^6}{0.87 \times 500 \times 0.9 \times 415} = 2024\text{ mm}^2 \implies 623\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 16 mm dia bars @ 150 mm c/c at top ($A_{st} = 1340\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$).
  • Column Strip Positive Moment ($60\%$ of $325.9 = 195.5\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$ at slab): $$A_{st} = \frac{195.5 \times 10^6}{0.87 \times 500 \times 0.9 \times 270} = 1851\text{ mm}^2 \implies 569\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 12 mm dia bars @ 140 mm c/c at bottom ($A_{st} = 808\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$).
  • Middle Strip Span Moment ($40\%$ of $325.9 = 130.4\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$): $$A_{st} = \frac{130.4 \times 10^6}{0.87 \times 500 \times 0.9 \times 270} = 1234\text{ mm}^2 \implies 380\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 12 mm dia bars @ 200 mm c/c at bottom.
Eg Exterior panels experience eccentric unbalanced shear transfer into edge columns, necessitating closed stirrups in the spandrel strip and 100% of top bars anchored with full development length into the exterior column.

topic: Intze Water Tank Complete Superstructure Design
question: Design the super structure of an Intze water tank with cylindrical walls of 11 m diameter and 5 m height. The rise of top and bottom dome is 2 m and 1.6 m respectively. The vertical height of conical dome is 2 m and diameter of ring girder at the junction of conical and bottom spherical dome is 7 m. Sketch the reinforcement details.
solution:
1. Dimensions & Material Specifications:
  • Cylindrical Wall: Diameter $D = 11\text{ m} \implies R_1 = 5.5\text{ m}$; Height $H = 5\text{ m}$
  • Top Dome: Rise $h_1 = 2.0\text{ m}$; Radius $R_{top} = \frac{5.5^2 + 2.0^2}{2 \times 2.0} = \frac{34.25}{4} = 8.56\text{ m}$
  • Conical Dome: Top dia $11\text{ m}$, Bottom dia $7\text{ m}$, Height $H_c = 2\text{ m} \implies \tan\alpha = 1.0 \implies \alpha = 45^\circ$
  • Bottom Dome: Base dia $7\text{ m}$, Rise $h_2 = 1.6\text{ m} \implies R_{bot} = \frac{3.5^2 + 1.6^2}{2 \times 1.6} = 4.63\text{ m}$
  • Materials: M25 concrete ($\sigma_{cbc} = 8.5\text{ N/mm}^2, \sigma_{ct} = 1.3\text{ N/mm}^2$) and Fe 415 steel ($\sigma_{st} = 130\text{ N/mm}^2$ on liquid face, $190\text{ N/mm}^2$ elsewhere).
2. Component-by-Component Design:
  • Component 1: Top Spherical Dome ($t_1 = 100\text{ mm}$):
    • Self-weight + live load ($1.5\text{ kN/m}^2$): $w = (0.10 \times 25) + 1.5 = 4.0\text{ kN/m}^2$.
    • Semi-central angle: $\sin\theta_1 = \frac{5.5}{8.56} = 0.6425 \implies \theta_1 = 40.0^\circ, \cos\theta_1 = 0.766$.
    • Meridional Thrust at springing: $$T_1 = \frac{w R_{top}}{1 + \cos\theta_1} = \frac{4.0 \times 8.56}{1 + 0.766} = 19.39\text{ kN/m}$$
    • Meridional Compressive Stress: $\sigma = \frac{19.39 \times 10^3}{1000 \times 100} = 0.194\text{ N/mm}^2 \ll 8.5\text{ N/mm}^2$ [Safe].
    • Reinforcement: Minimum $0.24\% = 240\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$. Provide 8 mm dia bars @ 180 mm c/c both ways in mesh.
  • Component 2: Top Ring Beam ($B_1$ at top of cylindrical wall):
    • Inward horizontal thrust: $H_1 = T_1 \cos\theta_1 = 19.39 \times 0.766 = 14.85\text{ kN/m}$.
    • Hoop Tension: $T = H_1 \times \frac{D}{2} = 14.85 \times 5.5 = 81.68\text{ kN}$.
    • Steel required: $A_{st} = \frac{81.68 \times 10^3}{130} = 628\text{ mm}^2$. Provide 4 nos. 16 mm dia bars ($A_{st} = 804\text{ mm}^2$).
    • Size of Beam: $b \times D = 300\text{ mm} \times 350\text{ mm}$ with 8 mm 2-legged stirrups @ 200 mm c/c.
  • Component 3: Cylindrical Wall ($H = 5\text{ m}, D = 11\text{ m}$):
    • Maximum Hoop Tension at base: $T_{max} = \gamma_w H \frac{D}{2} = 10 \times 5.0 \times 5.5 = 275\text{ kN/m}$.
    • Hoop Steel: $A_{st} = \frac{275 \times 10^3}{130} = 2115\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$.
    • Provide 16 mm dia hoop rings @ 180 mm c/c on both faces ($A_{st, prov} = 2234\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$).
    • Wall thickness: $t = 30 H + 50 = 200\text{ mm}$. Check uncracked tensile stress: $$\sigma_{ct} = \frac{275000}{1000 \times 200 + 10 \times 2234} = 1.23\text{ N/mm}^2 < 1.3\text{ N/mm}^2 \quad \text{[Safe]}$$
  • Component 4: Conical Dome ($t_c = 250\text{ mm}, \alpha = 45^\circ$):
    • Transports total accumulated superstructure load ($W_T \approx 7850\text{ kN}$) into inward radial thrust.
    • Meridional thrust at base: $T_m = \frac{W_T}{\pi D_0 \sin\alpha} = \frac{7850}{\pi \times 7 \times 0.7071} = 505\text{ kN/m}$.
    • Meridional Compressive Stress: $\sigma = \frac{505 \times 10^3}{1000 \times 250} = 2.02\text{ N/mm}^2 \ll 8.5\text{ N/mm}^2$ [Safe]. Provide 12 mm dia bars @ 150 mm c/c along the slope.
  • Component 5: Bottom Spherical Dome ($t_b = 160\text{ mm}, R_2 = 4.63\text{ m}$):
    • Carries vertical water column above ($h_w \approx 5 + 2 = 7\text{ m}$) $\implies w = 70 + (0.16 \times 25) = 74\text{ kN/m}^2$.
    • Meridional thrust at springing: $T_2 = \frac{w R_2}{1 + \cos\theta_2} = \frac{74 \times 4.63}{1 + 0.6543} = 207\text{ kN/m}$.
    • Provide 10 mm dia bars @ 150 mm c/c both ways.
  • Component 6: Bottom Ring Girder ($B_2$ over 8 columns at $D_0 = 7\text{ m}$):
    • Net inward radial thrust $= 307.8\text{ kN/m} \implies$ Hoop Compression $= 1077\text{ kN}$.
    • Beam Size: $600\text{ mm} \times 900\text{ mm}$ with 8 nos. 25 mm dia bars and 10 mm 4-legged stirrups @ 150 mm c/c.
Eg Intze tanks are the most economical elevated reservoir design in India because balancing outward dome thrust with inward conical thrust drastically reduces ring beam sizes.

topic: RCC Square Bunker Design for Cement
question: Design a RCC square bunker to store 1000 kN of cement surcharged at 20°. The density of cement is 14.6 kN/m³ and its coefficient of internal friction is 0.321. Sketch the reinforcement detail.
solution:
1. Storage Capacity & Bunker Dimensions:
  • Capacity $W = 1000\text{ kN}$; Stored Material (Cement): Density $\gamma = 14.6\text{ kN/m}^3$
  • Coefficient of internal friction: $\mu = \tan\phi = 0.321 \implies \phi = 17.8^\circ \approx 18^\circ$
  • Surcharge angle: $\beta = 20^\circ \approx \phi$. Surcharged Rankine active coefficient: $$K_a = \cos\beta \frac{\cos\beta - \sqrt{\cos^2\beta - \cos^2\phi}}{\cos\beta + \sqrt{\cos^2\beta - \cos^2\phi}} \approx \cos\phi \approx \cos 18^\circ = 0.951$$
  • Volume required: $V = \frac{W}{\gamma} = \frac{1000}{14.6} = 68.5\text{ m}^3$
  • Assume square plan: $a \times a = 3.6\text{ m} \times 3.6\text{ m}$ ($A = 12.96\text{ m}^2$)
  • Hopper depth ($h_h$): With discharge opening $0.5\text{ m} \times 0.5\text{ m}$ and slope $\theta = 45^\circ$: $$h_h = \frac{3.6 - 0.5}{2} = 1.55\text{ m}$$ $$V_{hopper} = \frac{1.55}{3} [3.6^2 + 0.5^2 + 3.6 \times 0.5] = 0.517 [12.96 + 0.25 + 1.8] = 7.76\text{ m}^3$$
  • Volume in vertical portion: $V_v = 68.5 - 7.76 = 60.74\text{ m}^3$
  • Vertical wall height: $$H_v = \frac{V_v}{A} = \frac{60.74}{12.96} = 4.69\text{ m} \approx 4.8\text{ m}$$
2. Lateral Pressures & Wall Design:
  • Maximum horizontal pressure at base of vertical wall ($h = 4.8\text{ m}$): $$p_h = K_a \gamma H_v = 0.951 \times 14.6 \times 4.8 = 66.65\text{ kN/m}^2$$
  • Fixed End Moment at corners of continuous square frame: $$M_{corner} = \frac{p_h a^2}{12} = \frac{66.65 \times 3.6^2}{12} = 71.98\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Mid-span Positive Moment: $$M_{mid} = \frac{p_h a^2}{24} = \frac{66.65 \times 3.6^2}{24} = 35.99\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Direct Tension in wall per metre height: $$T = p_h \times \frac{a}{2} = 66.65 \times 1.8 = 119.97\text{ kN}$$
3. Section Sizing & Reinforcement:
  • Wall thickness: $t = 200\text{ mm}$ ($d = 165\text{ mm}$).
  • Tensile steel at corner ($f_y = 415\text{ N/mm}^2, \sigma_{st} = 130\text{ N/mm}^2$): $$A_{st, corner} = \frac{M}{\sigma_{st} \cdot j \cdot d} + \frac{T}{\sigma_{st}} = \frac{71.98 \times 10^6}{130 \times 0.85 \times 165} + \frac{119.97 \times 10^3}{130} = 3949 + 923 = 4872\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 20 mm dia bars @ 120 mm c/c on both faces ($A_{st, prov} = 5236\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$) at corner haunches.
  • Mid-span outer steel: Provide 16 mm dia bars @ 140 mm c/c ($A_{st} = 1436\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$).
  • Vertical steel: Minimum $0.24\% = 480\text{ mm}^2/\text{m} \implies$ 10 mm dia bars @ 160 mm c/c on both faces.
Eg Cement has a tendency to pack under high overburden pressure; hoppers must be lined with low-friction tiles or ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene liners to avoid arching.

  • Hopper depth ($h_h$): With discharge opening $0.5\text{ m} \times 0.5\text{ m}$ and slope $\theta = 45^\circ$: $$h_h = \frac{3.6 - 0.5}{2} = 1.55\text{ m}$$ $$V_{hopper} = \frac{1.55}{3} [3.6^2 + 0.5^2 + 3.6 \times 0.5] = 0.517 [12.96 + 0.25 + 1.8] = 7.76\text{ m}^3$$
  • Volume in vertical portion: $V_v = 68.5 - 7.76 = 60.74\text{ m}^3$
  • Vertical wall height: $$H_v = \frac{V_v}{A} = \frac{60.74}{12.96} = 4.69\text{ m} \approx 4.8\text{ m}$$
2. Lateral Pressures & Wall Design:
  • Maximum horizontal pressure at base of vertical wall ($h = 4.8\text{ m}$): $$p_h = K_a \gamma H_v = 0.951 \times 14.6 \times 4.8 = 66.65\text{ kN/m}^2$$
  • Fixed End Moment at corners of continuous square frame: $$M_{corner} = \frac{p_h a^2}{12} = \frac{66.65 \times 3.6^2}{12} = 71.98\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Mid-span Positive Moment: $$M_{mid} = \frac{p_h a^2}{24} = \frac{66.65 \times 3.6^2}{24} = 35.99\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Direct Tension in wall per metre height: $$T = p_h \times \frac{a}{2} = 66.65 \times 1.8 = 119.97\text{ kN}$$
3. Section Sizing & Reinforcement:
  • Wall thickness: $t = 200\text{ mm}$ ($d = 165\text{ mm}$).
  • Tensile steel at corner ($f_y = 415\text{ N/mm}^2, \sigma_{st} = 130\text{ N/mm}^2$): $$A_{st, corner} = \frac{M}{\sigma_{st} \cdot j \cdot d} + \frac{T}{\sigma_{st}} = \frac{71.98 \times 10^6}{130 \times 0.85 \times 165} + \frac{119.97 \times 10^3}{130} = 3949 + 923 = 4872\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 20 mm dia bars @ 120 mm c/c on both faces ($A_{st, prov} = 5236\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$) at corner haunches.

  • Vertical steel: Minimum $0.24\% = 480\text{ mm}^2/\text{m} \implies$ 10 mm dia bars @ 160 mm c/c on both faces.
Eg Cement has a tendency to pack under high overburden pressure; hoppers must be lined with low-friction tiles or ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene liners to avoid arching.

topic: Janssen's Horizontal Stress Intensity Derivation
question:
Using Janssen's theory, derive that the horizontal stress intensity for the bin is given by:
p_h = \frac{w r}{\mu'} \left[ 1 - e^{-\frac{\mu' K h}{r}} \right]
solution:
1. Differential Slice Equilibrium Formulation:
  • Consider a thin horizontal slice of granular material in a deep cylindrical bin of cross-sectional area $A$, perimeter $U$, and hydraulic radius $r = \frac{A}{U}$:
    • Thickness of slice $= dh$, at depth $h$ below the top surface.
    • Vertical pressure acting on top face $= p_v$ (downward).
    • Vertical pressure acting on bottom face $= p_v + dp_v$ (upward).
    • Downward gravity weight of the slice $= w \cdot A \cdot dh$ (where $w$ is unit weight of stored material).
    • Upward frictional resistance along the perimeter $= \mu' \cdot p_h \cdot U \cdot dh$ (where $\mu'$ is coefficient of wall friction and $p_h$ is lateral pressure).
2. Vertical Force Balance:
  • Equating vertical forces on the element ($\sum F_v = 0$): $$p_v A + w A dh = (p_v + dp_v) A + \mu' p_h U dh$$
  • Canceling $p_v A$ and dividing through by $A dh$: $$w - \frac{dp_v}{dh} - \mu' p_h \frac{U}{A} = 0$$
  • Substitute hydraulic radius $r = \frac{A}{U} \implies \frac{U}{A} = \frac{1}{r}$: $$\frac{dp_v}{dh} = w - \frac{\mu' p_h}{r}$$
  • Using Janssen's pressure ratio $K = \frac{p_h}{p_v} \implies p_h = K p_v$: $$\frac{dp_v}{dh} = w - \frac{\mu' K}{r} p_v$$
3. Differential Equation Solution & Boundary Condition:
  • Rearranging into standard first-order separable form: $$\frac{dp_v}{w - \frac{\mu' K}{r} p_v} = dh$$
  • Integrating both sides: $$-\frac{r}{\mu' K} \ln\left( w - \frac{\mu' K}{r} p_v \right) = h + C$$
  • Applying Boundary Condition at top surface: At $h = 0$, $p_v = 0$: $$C = -\frac{r}{\mu' K} \ln(w)$$
  • Substituting $C$ back into the integral: $$\ln\left( \frac{w - \frac{\mu' K}{r} p_v}{w} \right) = -\frac{\mu' K h}{r}$$ $$1 - \frac{\mu' K}{r w} p_v = e^{-\frac{\mu' K h}{r}}$$ $$p_v = \frac{w r}{\mu' K} \left[ 1 - e^{-\frac{\mu' K h}{r}} \right]$$
  • Since $p_h = K p_v$, multiplying by $K$ yields the final Janssen's horizontal stress formula: $$p_h = \frac{w r}{\mu'} \left[ 1 - e^{-\frac{\mu' K h}{r}} \right]$$
Eg As depth $h \to \infty$, the exponential term vanishes and $p_h \to \frac{w r}{\mu'}$, proving that deep silos reach a constant limiting lateral pressure regardless of additional height.

topic: Underground Rectangular Tank with High Water Table
question: Design underground rectangular water tank of dimensions 10 m * 4 m * 3.5 m with free board of 0.3 m. The dry density of soil is 17 kN/m³ and angle of internal friction is 30°. Water level is going up to ground. Use M25 grade of concrete and Fe415 steel. Sketch the reinforcement details.
solution:
1. Design Conditions & Critical Loading States:
  • Dimensions: $L = 10\text{ m}, B = 4\text{ m}, H = 3.5\text{ m}$, Freeboard $FB = 0.3\text{ m} \implies$ Water depth $h = 3.2\text{ m}$
  • Soil & Groundwater: $\gamma_{dry} = 17\text{ kN/m}^3, \phi = 30^\circ \implies K_a = \frac{1 - \sin 30^\circ}{1 + \sin 30^\circ} = \frac{1}{3}$. Saturated soil density $\gamma_{sat} \approx 20\text{ kN/m}^3 \implies \gamma' = 20 - 10 = 10\text{ kN/m}^3$. Water table at ground level.
  • Two Critical Design Cases:
    • Case A (Tank Full, No Earth Outside): Hydrostatic water pressure inside $p = \gamma_w h = 10 \times 3.2 = 32\text{ kN/m}^2$.
    • Case B (Tank Empty, Full Saturated Earth Pressure Outside): $$p_{ext} = K_a \gamma' H + \gamma_w H = \left(\frac{1}{3} \times 10 \times 3.5\right) + (10 \times 3.5) = 11.67 + 35.0 = 46.67\text{ kN/m}^2$$ Case B produces the maximum inward bending moment and governs wall thickness!
  • Aspect Ratio: $\frac{L}{B} = \frac{10}{4} = 2.5 > 2.0 \implies$ Long wall behaves as a vertical cantilever fixed at base raft; Short wall spans horizontally between long walls.
2. Structural Analysis of Long Walls ($L = 10\text{ m}$, Cantilever Action):
  • Because $L/B > 2$, long wall acts as a vertical cantilever of height $H = 3.5\text{ m}$.
  • Maximum Inward Bending Moment at Base (Case B, Tank Empty): $$M_{cant} = \frac{1}{6} K_a \gamma' H^3 + \frac{1}{6} \gamma_w H^3 = \frac{1}{6} p_{ext} H^2 = \frac{1}{6} \times 46.67 \times 3.5^2 = 95.28\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m/m}$$
  • Maximum Outward Moment at Base (Case A, Tank Full): $$M_{int} = \frac{1}{6} \gamma_w h^3 = \frac{1}{6} \times 10 \times 3.2^3 = 54.61\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m/m}$$
  • Effective Depth required on uncracked basis ($Q = 1.15\text{ N/mm}^2$): $$d = \sqrt{\frac{95.28 \times 10^6}{1000 \times 1.15}} = 287.8\text{ mm} \implies \text{Adopt overall thickness } D = 350\text{ mm } (d = 310\text{ mm})$$
  • Vertical Tensile Reinforcement at base of long wall (Inside face for Case B): $$A_{st} = \frac{M_{cant}}{\sigma_{st} \cdot j \cdot d} = \frac{95.28 \times 10^6}{130 \times 0.85 \times 310} = 2781\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 20 mm dia vertical bars @ 110 mm c/c ($A_{st} = 2856\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$) on inner face.
  • Vertical Steel on Outer face (for Case A full water): $$A_{st} = \frac{54.61 \times 10^6}{130 \times 0.85 \times 310} = 1594\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 16 mm dia vertical bars @ 125 mm c/c ($A_{st} = 1608\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$) on outer face.
3. Short Wall Analysis ($B = 4\text{ m}$, Horizontal Beam Action):
  • Short wall is supported at ends by long walls; spans horizontally with $B = 4\text{ m}$.
  • Effective lateral pressure at mid-height ($y = 1.75\text{ m}$): $$p = K_a \gamma' y + \gamma_w y = \left(\frac{1}{3} \times 10 \times 1.75\right) + (10 \times 1.75) = 23.33\text{ kN/m}^2$$
  • Corner Support Moment: $$M_{corner} = \frac{p B^2}{12} = \frac{23.33 \times 4^2}{12} = 31.11\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Mid-span Moment: $$M_{mid} = \frac{p B^2}{24} = \frac{23.33 \times 4^2}{24} = 15.55\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Horizontal Steel: Provide 16 mm dia bars @ 140 mm c/c at corners and 12 mm dia bars @ 150 mm c/c at mid-span.
4. Uplift Stability Check:
  • Total upward hydrostatic buoyant force on base raft ($10.7\text{ m} \times 4.7\text{ m} \times 3.5\text{ m}$): $$F_{buoyancy} = 10.7 \times 4.7 \times 3.5 \times 10 = 1760.1\text{ kN}$$
  • Self-weight of empty tank (walls + base raft $450\text{ mm}$ + roof slab $150\text{ mm}$): $$W_{empty} \approx 2150\text{ kN} > 1.2 \times F_{buoyancy} \implies \text{Safe against hydraulic floatation without anchors.}$$
Eg When water table rises to ground level, total lateral pressure increases more than threefold due to full hydrostatic water head plus submerged buoyant earth pressure.

topic: Interior Panel Flat Slab Design (7m x 7m)
question: Design the interior panel of flat slab 7 m * 7 m in size, for the super imposed load of 5 kN/m². Provide two-way reinforcements. Use M25 concrete and Fe500 steel. Sketch the reinforcement details.
solution:
1. Preliminary Proportions (IS 456 Direct Design Method):
  • Panel: Square $L_1 = L_2 = 7.0\text{ m}$; Superimposed Live Load $LL = 5.0\text{ kN/m}^2$, Floor finish $FF = 1.0\text{ kN/m}^2$
  • Column Head Dia ($D_c$): $D_c = 0.25 L = 0.25 \times 7.0 = 1.75\text{ m}$
  • Drop Dimensions: $L_{drop} = \frac{L}{3} = \frac{7.0}{3} = 2.33\text{ m} \implies$ Adopt square drop $2.6\text{ m} \times 2.6\text{ m}$
  • Slab Thickness ($t_s$): Based on deflection control ($L/32$): $$t_s = \frac{7000}{32} \approx 218\text{ mm} \implies \text{Adopt } t_s = 220\text{ mm}$$
  • Drop Thickness: Overall depth through drop $D_{drop} = 1.35 t_s = 1.35 \times 220 \approx 300\text{ mm}$ (drop projection = $80\text{ mm}$)
  • Design Factored Load:
    • Slab self-weight: $0.22 \times 25 = 5.5\text{ kN/m}^2$
    • Drop weight averaged: $\approx 0.35\text{ kN/m}^2$
    • Factored load: $w_u = 1.5 \times (5.5 + 0.35 + 1.0 + 5.0) = 1.5 \times 11.85 = 17.78\text{ kN/m}^2$.
2. Total Static Design Moment ($M_0$):
  • Clear Span $L_n$: $$L_n = L_1 - D_c = 7.0 - 1.75 = 5.25\text{ m} \ge 0.65 L_1 = 4.55\text{ m} \quad \text{[OK]}$$
  • Total Design Moment per Panel (IS 456 Cl. 31.4.2.2): $$W = w_u \times L_2 \times L_n = 17.78 \times 7.0 \times 5.25 = 653.4\text{ kN}$$ $$M_0 = \frac{W L_n}{8} = \frac{653.4 \times 5.25}{8} = 428.8\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Apportionment for Interior Panel:
    • Negative Design Moment: $M_{u,-} = 0.65 M_0 = 0.65 \times 428.8 = 278.7\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$
    • Positive Design Moment: $M_{u,+} = 0.35 M_0 = 0.35 \times 428.8 = 150.1\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$
3. Strip Moments & Steel Distribution:
  • Strip Widths: Column Strip $= 3.5\text{ m}$; Middle Strip $= 3.5\text{ m}$.
  • Column Strip Negative Moment ($75\%$ of $278.7 = 209.0\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$ in drop $d = 265\text{ mm}$): $$A_{st} = \frac{209.0 \times 10^6}{0.87 \times 500 \times 0.9 \times 265} = 2013\text{ mm}^2 \implies 575\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 12 mm dia bars @ 190 mm c/c at top across the column strip.
  • Column Strip Positive Moment ($60\%$ of $150.1 = 90.06\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$ in slab $d = 185\text{ mm}$): $$A_{st} = \frac{90.06 \times 10^6}{0.87 \times 500 \times 0.9 \times 185} = 1243\text{ mm}^2 \implies 355\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 10 mm dia bars @ 220 mm c/c at bottom.
  • Middle Strip Negative Moment ($25\%$ of $278.7 = 69.68\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$): $$A_{st} = \frac{69.68 \times 10^6}{0.87 \times 500 \times 0.9 \times 185} = 962\text{ mm}^2 \implies 275\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 10 mm dia bars @ 280 mm c/c at top.
  • Middle Strip Positive Moment ($40\%$ of $150.1 = 60.04\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$): Provide 10 mm dia bars @ 280 mm c/c at bottom.
4. Punching Shear Check:
  • Critical perimeter $b_0 = \pi (D_c + d) = \pi (1750 + 265) = 6330\text{ mm}$.
  • Punching Shear: $V_u = 17.78 \times (49 - \frac{\pi}{4} \times 2.015^2) = 17.78 \times (49 - 3.19) = 814.5\text{ kN}$.
  • $\tau_v = \frac{814.5 \times 10^3}{6330 \times 265} = 0.486\text{ N/mm}^2 < \tau_c = 0.25 \sqrt{25} = 1.25\text{ N/mm}^2$ [Extremely Safe].
Eg Direct Design Method requires at least three continuous spans in each direction with panel aspect ratio $L/B \le 2.0$ and live-to-dead load ratio $\le 3.0$.

  • Punching Shear: $V_u = 17.78 \times (49 - \frac{\pi}{4} \times 2.015^2) = 17.78 \times (49 - 3.19) = 814.5\text{ kN}$.
  • $\tau_v = \frac{814.5 \times 10^3}{6330 \times 265} = 0.486\text{ N/mm}^2 < \tau_c = 0.25 \sqrt{25} = 1.25\text{ N/mm}^2$ [Extremely Safe].
Eg Direct Design Method requires at least three continuous spans in each direction with panel aspect ratio $L/B \le 2.0$ and live-to-dead load ratio $\le 3.0$.

topic: Grid Slab Design (10m x 12m by Rankine-Grashoff)
question: Design a grid slab to cover a floor area of 10 m * 12 m. The spacing of the ribs in mutually perpendicular direction being 2 m c/c. Live is load 1.8 kN/m². Adopt M20 grade of concrete and Fe500 steel by using approximate method (Rankine Grasshoff theory). Sketch the reinforcement details.
solution:
1. Geometric Dimensions & Design Loads:
  • Floor Area: Short span $L_x = 10\text{ m}$, Long span $L_y = 12\text{ m}$
  • Rib Spacing: $s_x = s_y = 2.0\text{ m}$ c/c
  • Topping slab thickness: $t_s = 80\text{ mm}$
  • Trial Rib Dimensions: Width $b_w = 180\text{ mm}$, Depth $D = 600\text{ mm}$ ($d = 550\text{ mm}$)
  • Loads per square metre:
    • Slab self-weight: $0.08 \times 25 = 2.0\text{ kN/m}^2$
    • Rib self-weight: $(0.60 - 0.08) \times 0.18 \times 25 \times \frac{2 + 2}{2 \times 2} = 2.34\text{ kN/m}^2$
    • Floor finish: $1.0\text{ kN/m}^2$; Live Load: $1.8\text{ kN/m}^2$
    • Total Characteristic Load: $q = 2.0 + 2.34 + 1.0 + 1.8 = 7.14\text{ kN/m}^2$
    • Factored Load: $q_u = 1.5 \times 7.14 = 10.71\text{ kN/m}^2$.
2. Rankine-Grashoff Load Partitioning:
  • Load transferred to short ribs ($q_{ux}$): $$q_{ux} = q_u \left( \frac{L_y^4}{L_x^4 + L_y^4} \right) = 10.71 \times \frac{12^4}{10^4 + 12^4} = 10.71 \times \frac{20736}{10000 + 20736} = 10.71 \times 0.6746 = 7.225\text{ kN/m}^2$$
  • Load transferred to long ribs ($q_{uy}$): $$q_{uy} = q_u - q_{ux} = 10.71 - 7.225 = 3.485\text{ kN/m}^2$$
  • Load per metre run on central short-span rib ($s = 2.0\text{ m}$): $$w_{ux} = q_{ux} \times s = 7.225 \times 2.0 = 14.45\text{ kN/m}$$
  • Load per metre run on central long-span rib: $$w_{uy} = q_{uy} \times s = 3.485 \times 2.0 = 6.97\text{ kN/m}$$
3. Maximum Moments & Rib Reinforcement:
  • Maximum Bending Moment in Short Rib ($L_x = 10\text{ m}$): $$M_{ux} = \frac{w_{ux} L_x^2}{8} = \frac{14.45 \times 10^2}{8} = 180.63\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Maximum Shear Force at Support: $$V_{ux} = \frac{w_{ux} L_x}{2} = \frac{14.45 \times 10}{2} = 72.25\text{ kN}$$
  • Flange Width: $b_f = 2000\text{ mm}$; Flange depth $D_f = 80\text{ mm}$. Neutral axis lies within flange $\implies$ Rectangular beam formula applies.
  • Tensile Reinforcement ($f_y = 500\text{ N/mm}^2, f_{ck} = 20\text{ N/mm}^2, d = 550\text{ mm}$): $$A_{st, x} = \frac{0.5 \times 20}{500} \left[ 1 - \sqrt{1 - \frac{4.59 \times 180.63 \times 10^6}{20 \times 2000 \times 550^2}} \right] \times 2000 \times 550 = 802\text{ mm}^2$$ Provide 3 nos. 20 mm dia bars ($A_{st, prov} = 942\text{ mm}^2$) in the tension zone.
  • Long Rib Reinforcement ($L_y = 12\text{ m}, M_{uy} = \frac{6.97 \times 12^2}{8} = 125.46\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$): $$A_{st, y} \approx 540\text{ mm}^2 \implies \text{Provide } \mathbf{3\text{ nos. } 16\text{ mm dia bars}} \ (A_{st} = 603\text{ mm}^2).$$
  • Shear Stirrups: $$\tau_v = \frac{72.25 \times 10^3}{180 \times 550} = 0.73\text{ N/mm}^2 > \tau_c = 0.58\text{ N/mm}^2$$ Provide 8 mm dia 2-legged stirrups @ 150 mm c/c near supports.
Eg Top slab between ribs functions as a two-way slab supported on four sides by the ribs, reinforced with an 8 mm mesh @ 150 mm c/c.

topic: Fixed-Base Circular Water Tank Design (400 kL)
question: Design a RC circular tank open at top and fixed at base resting on ground for a capacity of 400 kL resting on the ground by any method. Use M25 concrete and Fe415 steel.
solution:
1. Dimensions & Dimension Parameter:
  • Capacity $V = 400\text{ kL} = 400\text{ m}^3$; Assume water depth $H = 4.0\text{ m}$, Freeboard $FB = 0.3\text{ m}$
  • Plan Diameter: $$\frac{\pi}{4} D^2 \times 4.0 = 400 \implies D = \sqrt{\frac{400}{\pi}} = 11.28\text{ m} \approx 11.5\text{ m} \implies R = 5.75\text{ m}$$
  • Assume wall thickness $t = 200\text{ mm} = 0.20\text{ m}$
  • IS 3370 Dimension Parameter: $$\frac{H^2}{D t} = \frac{4.0^2}{11.5 \times 0.20} = \frac{16}{2.3} = 6.96 \approx 7.0$$
2. Tension & Moment Coefficients (IS 3370 Part IV Table 9 & 10 for Fixed Base, $H^2/Dt = 7$):
  • Maximum Hoop Tension occurs at depth $y = 0.6 H = 2.4\text{ m}$ from top: $$\text{Tension Coeff } = 0.532 \implies T_{max} = 0.532 \times \gamma_w H R = 0.532 \times 10 \times 4.0 \times 5.75 = 122.36\text{ kN/m}$$
  • Maximum Vertical Bending Moment at Base: $$\text{Moment Coeff } = -0.0146 \implies M_{base} = 0.0146 \times \gamma_w H^3 = 0.0146 \times 10 \times 4.0^3 = 9.34\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m/m}$$
3. Section Sizing & Reinforcement:
  • Hoop Reinforcement at $0.6 H$ ($\sigma_{st} = 130\text{ N/mm}^2$): $$A_{st, hoop} = \frac{T_{max}}{\sigma_{st}} = \frac{122.36 \times 10^3}{130} = 941\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 12 mm dia hoop rings @ 120 mm c/c ($A_{st} = 942\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$) arranged on outer face, with minimum distribution hoops on inner face.
  • Vertical Steel at Base for Bending Moment ($d = 200 - 35 = 165\text{ mm}$): $$A_{st, vert} = \frac{M_{base}}{\sigma_{st} \cdot j \cdot d} = \frac{9.34 \times 10^6}{130 \times 0.85 \times 165} = 512\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 10 mm dia vertical bars @ 150 mm c/c ($A_{st} = 523\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$) on water face at base.
  • Uncracked Concrete Tensile Stress: $$\sigma_{ct} = \frac{122360}{1000 \times 200 + 10 \times 942} = 0.584\text{ N/mm}^2 \ll 1.3\text{ N/mm}^2 \quad \text{[Safe & watertight]}$$
Eg Fixed base restraint eliminates hoop bursting tension at the very bottom of the wall, but requires vertical moment bars anchored into the foundation slab.

topic: Flexible-Base Circular Water Tank Design (350 kL)
question: Design of RC circular water tank resting on the ground and flexible at base for a capacity of 350 kL. Use M25 concrete and Fe500 steel.
solution:
1. Dimensions & Sizing:
  • Capacity $V = 350\text{ m}^3$; Assume water depth $H = 3.5\text{ m}$, Freeboard $FB = 0.3\text{ m}$
  • Diameter: $$\frac{\pi}{4} D^2 \times 3.5 = 350 \implies D = \sqrt{\frac{400}{\pi}} = 11.28\text{ m} \approx 11.3\text{ m} \implies R = 5.65\text{ m}$$
  • Flexible/sliding base means zero moment is induced at the base $\implies$ entire hydrostatic pressure is carried by pure hoop tension.
2. Maximum Hoop Tension & Steel Design:
  • Maximum hoop tension at bottom of wall ($H = 3.5\text{ m}$): $$T_{max} = \gamma_w H R = 10 \times 3.5 \times 5.65 = 197.75\text{ kN/m}$$
  • Hoop Steel Required ($\sigma_{st} = 130\text{ N/mm}^2$ for crack limit $w \le 0.1\text{ mm}$ in Fe 500 per IS 3370): $$A_{st, hoop} = \frac{197.75 \times 10^3}{130} = 1521\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$
  • Provide in 2 curtains: $760.5\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$ each face $\implies$ 12 mm dia hoop rings @ 140 mm c/c on both faces ($A_{st, prov} = 1616\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$).
  • Wall Thickness: $$t \ge \frac{T_{max}}{1000 \sigma_{ct}} = \frac{197750}{1000 \times 1.3} \approx 152\text{ mm} \implies \text{Adopt } t = 180\text{ mm}$$
  • Vertical Steel: $0.24\% = \frac{0.24}{100} \times 1000 \times 180 = 432\text{ mm}^2/\text{m} \implies$ 8 mm dia bars @ 200 mm c/c on both faces.
Eg A flexible joint using asphalt mastic pad completely relieves vertical bending moments, eliminating base cracking risks inherent in rigid ground connections.

topic: Engineering Differences Between Bunkers and Silos
question: Differentiate between bunker and silos.
solution:
1. Definitive Contrast Between Bunkers and Silos (IS 4995):
  • 1. Rupture Plane Criterion (Airy's / Coulomb Definition):
    • Bunker (Shallow Bin): The plane of rupture drawn from the bottom edge cuts the top horizontal grain surface ($h \le b \tan(45^\circ + \phi/2)$).
    • Silo (Deep Bin): The plane of rupture intersects the opposite vertical wall before reaching the top free surface ($h > b \tan(45^\circ + \phi/2)$).
  • 2. Lateral Pressure Theory & Distribution:
    • Bunker: Analyzed using Rankine's or Coulomb's earth pressure theory. Lateral pressure increases linearly with depth ($p_h = K_a \gamma h$).
    • Silo: Analyzed using Janssen's or Airy's deep bin theory. Lateral pressure increases asymptotically toward a maximum limit due to grain wall friction ($p_h \to \frac{\gamma R}{\mu'}$).
  • 3. Wall Friction & Load Transfer:
    • Bunker: Wall friction is negligible; bottom carries practically 100% of the total stored material weight.
    • Silo: Wall friction carries a major fraction (up to 60-70%) of total material weight, producing severe axial compression in the vertical walls.
  • 4. Geometric Aspect Ratio & Cross-Section:
    • Bunker: Shallow depth ($H < 2B$), typically square or rectangular with sloping hopper bottoms.
    • Silo: Very tall structure ($H \ge 3B$ to $5B$), predominantly circular to exploit hoop tension.
Eg Coal storage bunkers at thermal power plants are shallow rectangular bins, whereas wheat storage silos in grain terminals are 30 m tall circular concrete shafts.

topic: Step-by-Step Structural Design Procedure for Silos
question: Discuss the Design procedure of silo.
solution:
1. Silo Design Protocol (IS 4995 Parts I & II):
  • Step 1: Stored Material Characterization & Sizing:
    • Establish bulk unit weight $\gamma$, angle of internal friction $\phi$, angle of wall friction $\phi'$, and pressure ratio $K = \frac{1 - \sin\phi}{1 + \sin\phi}$.
    • Determine diameter $D$ and total height $H$ from required storage capacity $V = \frac{\pi}{4} D^2 H$.
  • Step 2: Pressure Calculations via Janssen's Equations:
    • Compute hydraulic radius $R = D/4$.
    • Compute horizontal pressure: $p_h = \frac{\gamma R}{\mu'} [1 - e^{-\mu' K h / R}]$.
    • Compute vertical grain pressure: $p_v = p_h / K$.
    • Apply dynamic discharge overpressure factor (typically $1.35$ to $1.75$ per IS 4995 Part I).
  • Step 3: Cylindrical Wall Reinforcement (Hoop Steel & Axial Compression):
    • Circumferential hoop steel: $A_{st, hoop} = \frac{T_{max}}{\sigma_{st}} = \frac{p_{h, des} (D/2)}{\sigma_{st}}$.
    • Total vertical load carried by wall due to wall friction: $W_w = \int_0^H \mu' p_h (\pi D) dh$.
    • Check axial compressive stress: $\sigma_{cc} = \frac{W_w + W_{self}}{\pi D t} \le \sigma_{cc, perm}$.
    • Provide vertical steel for combined axial compression and temperature distribution ($p \ge 0.3\%$).
  • Step 4: Hopper Bottom Design:
    • Slope angle $\theta \ge \phi + 15^\circ$ for free flow.
    • Design for meridional tension $T = \frac{W_{total}}{\pi D \sin\theta}$ and hoop tension.
  • Step 5: Columns & Staging:
    • Columns support the bottom ring girder and are designed for vertical dead/live loads plus lateral wind/seismic moments.
Eg Silo walls must be checked for buckling under vertical friction loads since over 60% of grain weight hangs on the concrete shell via friction.

topic: Carpenter's vs Reissner's Method for Fixed-Base Circular Tanks
question: Differentiate between carpenter's and Reissner's method of designing circular tanks with fixed at base.
solution:
1. Analytical Contrast: Carpenter's vs Reissner's Method:
  • 1. Theoretical Foundation & Formulation:
    • Carpenter's Method: Based on simplified beam-on-elastic-foundation and energy equilibrium principles. Treats vertical strips as cantilevers resisting a portion of hydrostatic pressure while ring hoops resist the balance through compatibility of radial deflections.
    • Reissner's Method: Based on classical cylindrical thin-shell theory solving the governing fourth-order differential equation: $$\frac{d^4 w}{d y^4} + 4 \beta^4 w = \frac{p(y)}{D}$$ where $\beta^4 = \frac{3(1 - \nu^2)}{R^2 t^2}$ is the shell damping characteristic.
  • 2. Boundary Condition Rigor:
    • Carpenter's Method: Uses approximated charts assuming idealized point rotations and piecewise moment distribution.
    • Reissner's Method: Enforces rigorous edge boundary conditions ($w = 0, \frac{dw}{dy} = 0$ at base) yielding exact damped sinusoidal decay curves for moment and shear from the base upward.
  • 3. Accuracy & Modern Standing:
    • Carpenter's Method: Simpler for preliminary hand calculations but loses accuracy when wall thickness varies or when $H^2 / Dt > 12$.
    • Reissner's Method: Highly accurate, mathematically exact, and forms the mathematical basis for IS 3370 (Part IV) design coefficient tables.
Eg Reissner's solution reveals that fixed-base moments attenuate rapidly within a height of $h_k = \frac{\pi}{\beta} \approx 2.5 \sqrt{R t}$ above the base raft.
