  • 2. Boundary Condition Rigor:
    • Carpenter's Method: Uses approximated charts assuming idealized point rotations and piecewise moment distribution.
    • Reissner's Method: Enforces rigorous edge boundary conditions ($w = 0, \frac{dw}{dy} = 0$ at base) yielding exact damped sinusoidal decay curves for moment and shear from the base upward.
  • 3. Accuracy & Modern Standing:
    • Carpenter's Method: Simpler for preliminary hand calculations but loses accuracy when wall thickness varies or when $H^2 / Dt > 12$.
    • Reissner's Method: Highly accurate, mathematically exact, and forms the mathematical basis for IS 3370 (Part IV) design coefficient tables.
Eg Reissner's solution reveals that fixed-base moments attenuate rapidly within a height of $h_k = \frac{\pi}{\beta} \approx 2.5 \sqrt{R t}$ above the base raft.

topic: Intze Tank Superstructure (12m dia x 6m ht)
question: Design the super structure of an Intze water tank with cylindrical walls of 12 m diameter and 6 m height. The rise of top and bottom dome is 2.4 m and 1.4 m respectively. The vertical height of conical dome is 2.5 m and diameter of ring girder at the junction of conical and bottom spherical dome is 7 m.
solution:
1. Dimensions & Proportions:
  • Cylindrical Wall: $D = 12\text{ m} \implies R_1 = 6\text{ m}$; Height $H = 6\text{ m}$
  • Top Spherical Dome: Rise $h_1 = 2.4\text{ m} \implies R_{top} = \frac{6^2 + 2.4^2}{2 \times 2.4} = \frac{41.76}{4.8} = 8.70\text{ m}$
  • Conical Dome: Top dia $12\text{ m}$, Bottom dia $7\text{ m}$, Height $H_c = 2.5\text{ m} \implies \tan\alpha = \frac{2.5}{2.5} = 1.0 \implies \alpha = 45^\circ$
  • Bottom Dome: Base dia $7\text{ m}$, Rise $h_2 = 1.4\text{ m} \implies R_{bot} = \frac{3.5^2 + 1.4^2}{2 \times 1.4} = \frac{14.21}{2.8} = 5.075\text{ m}$
  • Materials: M25 concrete and Fe 415 steel ($\sigma_{st} = 130\text{ N/mm}^2$ on liquid face, $190\text{ N/mm}^2$ elsewhere).
2. Component-by-Component Design:
  • 1. Top Dome ($t = 100\text{ mm}$):
    • Total load $w = 2.5 + 1.5 = 4.0\text{ kN/m}^2$. $\sin\theta_1 = 6 / 8.7 = 0.6897 \implies \theta_1 = 43.6^\circ, \cos\theta_1 = 0.724$.
    • Meridional thrust: $T_1 = \frac{w R_{top}}{1 + \cos\theta_1} = \frac{4.0 \times 8.7}{1 + 0.724} = 20.19\text{ kN/m}$.
    • Stress: $\sigma = 0.202\text{ N/mm}^2 \ll 8.5\text{ N/mm}^2$ [Safe]. Provide 8 mm dia bars @ 180 mm c/c mesh.
  • 2. Top Ring Beam ($B_1$):
    • Inward horizontal thrust: $H_1 = 20.19 \times 0.724 = 14.62\text{ kN/m}$.
    • Hoop Tension: $T = 14.62 \times 6 = 87.72\text{ kN}$.
    • Steel: $A_{st} = \frac{87.72 \times 10^3}{130} = 675\text{ mm}^2 \implies$ Provide 4 nos. 16 mm dia bars ($A_{st} = 804\text{ mm}^2$).
    • Size: $300\text{ mm} \times 350\text{ mm}$ with 8 mm stirrups @ 180 mm c/c.
  • 3. Cylindrical Wall ($H = 6\text{ m}, D = 12\text{ m}$):
    • Maximum Hoop Tension at base: $T_{max} = \gamma_w H \frac{D}{2} = 10 \times 6.0 \times 6.0 = 360\text{ kN/m}$.
    • Hoop Steel: $A_{st} = \frac{360 \times 10^3}{130} = 2769\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$.
    • Provide 20 mm dia hoop rings @ 180 mm c/c on both faces ($A_{st, prov} = 3490\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$).
    • Thickness: $t = 30 \times 6 + 50 = 230\text{ mm}$. Check uncracked tension: $$\sigma_{ct} = \frac{360000}{1000 \times 230 + 10 \times 3490} = 1.36\text{ N/mm}^2 \approx 1.3\text{ N/mm}^2 \implies \text{Adopt } t = 250\text{ mm}.$$
  • 4. Conical Dome & Bottom Dome ($t_c = 250\text{ mm}, t_b = 160\text{ mm}$):
    • Conical dome carries cumulative weight $\approx 10200\text{ kN}$ into inward thrust.
    • Provide 16 mm dia bars @ 150 mm c/c along the conical slope.
    • Bottom dome carries water head $\approx 8.5\text{ m}$; provide 12 mm dia bars @ 140 mm c/c both ways.
  • 5. Bottom Ring Girder ($B_2$ over 8 columns at $D_0 = 7\text{ m}$):
    • Net inward radial thrust $\approx 350\text{ kN/m} \implies$ Hoop Compression $= 1225\text{ kN}$.
    • Beam size: $600\text{ mm} \times 1000\text{ mm}$ with 8 nos. 25 mm dia bars and 10 mm 4-legged stirrups @ 150 mm c/c.
Eg For a 12 m diameter tank holding over 700 kL, the bottom ring girder acts as a continuous circular curved beam resisting combined torsion, negative moments over columns, and hoop compression.

topic: RCC Square Bunker for Wheat (SBC 160 kN/m²)
question: Design a RCC square bunker to store 800 kN of wheat surcharged at angle of repose. The density of wheat is 8.5 kN/m³ and its coefficient of friction is 0.466. Bearing capacity of soil is 160 kN/m² and basic wind pressure is 1.5 kN/m².
solution:
1. Dimensions & Storage Sizing:
  • Capacity $W = 800\text{ kN}$; Stored Material (Wheat): Density $\gamma = 8.5\text{ kN/m}^3$, $\mu = \tan\phi = 0.466 \implies \phi = 25^\circ$
  • Volume of wheat: $V = \frac{800}{8.5} = 94.12\text{ m}^3$
  • Square plan size: Adopt $a \times a = 4.0\text{ m} \times 4.0\text{ m}$ ($A = 16.0\text{ m}^2$)
  • Hopper depth with discharge opening $0.5\text{ m} \times 0.5\text{ m}$ and $\theta = 45^\circ$: $$h_h = \frac{4.0 - 0.5}{2} = 1.75\text{ m}$$ $$V_h = \frac{1.75}{3} [4.0^2 + 0.5^2 + 4.0 \times 0.5] = 0.583 [16 + 0.25 + 2.0] = 10.64\text{ m}^3$$
  • Vertical portion volume: $V_v = 94.12 - 10.64 = 83.48\text{ m}^3$
  • Height of vertical walls: $$H_v = \frac{V_v}{A} = \frac{83.48}{16.0} = 5.22\text{ m} \approx 5.25\text{ m}$$
  • Rankine active earth pressure coefficient with surcharge $\beta = \phi = 25^\circ$: $$K_a = \cos\phi = \cos 25^\circ = 0.906$$
2. Pressures & Wall Moments:
  • Maximum horizontal pressure at base of vertical wall ($h = 5.25\text{ m}$): $$p_h = K_a \gamma H_v = 0.906 \times 8.5 \times 5.25 = 40.43\text{ kN/m}^2$$
  • Continuous horizontal frame moments: $$M_{corner} = \frac{p_h a^2}{12} = \frac{40.43 \times 4.0^2}{12} = 53.91\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$ $$M_{mid} = \frac{p_h a^2}{24} = 26.95\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Direct Tension in wall per metre height: $$T = p_h \times \frac{a}{2} = 40.43 \times 2.0 = 80.86\text{ kN}$$
3. Section Sizing & Reinforcement:
  • Adopt wall thickness $t = 180\text{ mm}$ ($d = 145\text{ mm}$) in M25 concrete ($f_y = 415\text{ N/mm}^2, \sigma_{st} = 130\text{ N/mm}^2$).
  • Corner Negative Steel: $$A_{st, corner} = \frac{53.91 \times 10^6}{130 \times 0.85 \times 145} + \frac{80.86 \times 10^3}{130} = 3364 + 622 = 3986\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 20 mm dia bars @ 150 mm c/c on both faces ($A_{st} = 4188\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$) at corner haunches.
  • Mid-span Outer Steel: Provide 16 mm dia bars @ 150 mm c/c ($A_{st} = 1340\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$).
  • Hopper Bottom: Slab thickness $t = 160\text{ mm}$; provide 12 mm dia bars @ 140 mm c/c horizontally and 10 mm dia bars @ 160 mm c/c along the slope.
  • Staging Columns & Isolated Footings: 4 corner columns designed for vertical gravity loads + wind overturning moments ($p_{wind} = 1.5\text{ kN/m}^2$), sized at $450\text{ mm} \times 450\text{ mm}$ with footing area $A \approx 3.0\text{ m} \times 3.0\text{ m}$ to keep bearing pressure $\le 160\text{ kN/m}^2$.
Eg Wind pressure of 1.5 kN/m² acting on the exposed vertical and hopper bunker faces creates significant lateral shear that must be braced across the 4 corner staging columns.

topic: Interior Panel Flat Slab Design (5m x 6m)
question: Design the interior panel of flat slab (slab with drop and column with column head) 5 m * 6 m in size, for the super imposed load of 6 kN/m². Provide two way reinforcements. Use M20 concrete and Fe415 steel. Sketch the reinforcement details.
solution:
1. Dimensions & Preliminary Proportions:
  • Panel Dimensions: $L_1 = 6.0\text{ m}$ (span in direction of moments considered), $L_2 = 5.0\text{ m}$ (transverse span)
  • Superimposed Load: $LL = 6.0\text{ kN/m}^2$, Floor finish $FF = 1.0\text{ kN/m}^2$
  • Column Head Dia: $D_c = 0.25 L = 0.25 \times 6.0 = 1.5\text{ m}$
  • Drop Dimensions: $L_{drop, 1} = \frac{6.0}{3} = 2.0\text{ m}$, $L_{drop, 2} = \frac{5.0}{3} = 1.67\text{ m} \implies$ Adopt drop $2.2\text{ m} \times 2.0\text{ m}$
  • Slab Thickness: Deflection control with drops $\implies t_s = \frac{6000}{32} \approx 188\text{ mm} \implies$ Adopt $t_s = 200\text{ mm}$
  • Drop Thickness: Overall depth through drop $D_{drop} = 260\text{ mm}$ (projection = $60\text{ mm}$)
  • Design Loads:
    • Slab self-weight: $0.20 \times 25 = 5.0\text{ kN/m}^2$
    • Drop excess weight averaged: $\approx 0.30\text{ kN/m}^2$
    • Factored load: $w_u = 1.5 \times (5.0 + 0.30 + 1.0 + 6.0) = 1.5 \times 12.3 = 18.45\text{ kN/m}^2$.
2. Total Design Moment ($M_0$) in Long Direction:
  • Clear Span $L_n = L_1 - D_c = 6.0 - 1.5 = 4.5\text{ m} \ge 0.65 L_1 = 3.9\text{ m}$
  • Total Design Moment: $$W = w_u \times L_2 \times L_n = 18.45 \times 5.0 \times 4.5 = 415.13\text{ kN}$$ $$M_0 = \frac{W L_n}{8} = \frac{415.13 \times 4.5}{8} = 233.51\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Apportionment for Interior Panel:
    • Total Negative Moment: $M_{u,-} = 0.65 M_0 = 0.65 \times 233.51 = 151.78\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$
    • Total Positive Moment: $M_{u,+} = 0.35 M_0 = 0.35 \times 233.51 = 81.73\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$
3. Strip Moments & Steel Distribution:
  • Strip Widths: Column Strip $= 0.5 L_2 = 2.5\text{ m}$; Middle Strip $= 2.5\text{ m}$.
  • Column Strip Negative Moment ($75\%$ of $151.78 = 113.84\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$ at drop $d = 225\text{ mm}$): $$A_{st} = \frac{113.84 \times 10^6}{0.87 \times 415 \times 0.9 \times 225} = 1558\text{ mm}^2 \implies 623\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 12 mm dia bars @ 180 mm c/c at top across the column strip.
  • Column Strip Positive Moment ($60\%$ of $81.73 = 49.04\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$ in slab $d = 165\text{ mm}$): $$A_{st} = \frac{49.04 \times 10^6}{0.87 \times 415 \times 0.9 \times 165} = 914\text{ mm}^2 \implies 366\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 10 mm dia bars @ 210 mm c/c at bottom across column strip.
  • Middle Strip Negative ($25\%$ of $151.78 = 37.95\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$): Provide 10 mm dia bars @ 260 mm c/c at top.
  • Middle Strip Positive ($40\%$ of $81.73 = 32.69\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$): Provide 10 mm dia bars @ 260 mm c/c at bottom.
4. Punching Shear Check:
  • $b_0 = \pi (D_c + d) = \pi (1500 + 225) = 5419\text{ mm}$.
  • $V_u = 18.45 \times (30 - \frac{\pi}{4} \times 1.725^2) = 18.45 \times (30 - 2.34) = 510.3\text{ kN}$.
  • $\tau_v = \frac{510.3 \times 10^3}{5419 \times 225} = 0.419\text{ N/mm}^2 < \tau_c = 0.25 \sqrt{20} = 1.118\text{ N/mm}^2$ [Safe].
Eg Rectangular flat slab panels ($5\text{ m} \times 6\text{ m}$) require moments to be calculated independently in both directions, using $L_n = 4.5\text{ m}$ for the long span and $L_n = 3.5\text{ m}$ for the short span.

topic: Fixed-Base Circular Water Tank Design (450 kL)
question: Design a circular tank for capacity of 450 kL resting on the ground. The walls are fixed at base and free at top. Use M25 concrete and Fe415 steel.
solution:
1. Dimensions & Ratio Formulation:
  • Capacity $V = 450\text{ kL} = 450\text{ m}^3$; Assume water depth $H = 4.5\text{ m}$, Freeboard $FB = 0.3\text{ m}$
  • Diameter: $$\frac{\pi}{4} D^2 \times 4.5 = 450 \implies D = \sqrt{\frac{400}{\pi}} = 11.28\text{ m} \approx 11.5\text{ m} \implies R = 5.75\text{ m}$$
  • Trial Wall Thickness: $t = 220\text{ mm} = 0.22\text{ m}$
  • Dimension Parameter: $$\frac{H^2}{D t} = \frac{4.5^2}{11.5 \times 0.22} = \frac{20.25}{2.53} = 8.0$$
2. Internal Actions (IS 3370 Part IV Coefficients for $H^2 / Dt = 8$):

topic: Grid Slab Design (9m x 12.6m by Rankine-Grashoff)
question: Design a grid slab to cover a floor area of 9 m* 12.6 m. The spacing of the ribs in mutually perpendicular direction being 1.8 m c/c. Live is load 1.5 kN/m². Adopt M20 grade of concrete and Fe 415 steel by using approximate method (Rankine Grasshoff theory).
solution:
1. Dimensions & Load Allocation:
  • Dimensions: Short span $L_x = 9.0\text{ m}$, Long span $L_y = 12.6\text{ m}$
  • Rib Spacing: $s_x = s_y = 1.8\text{ m}$ c/c
  • Topping slab: $t_s = 80\text{ mm}$; Rib size: Width $b_w = 150\text{ mm}$, Depth $D = 550\text{ mm}$ ($d = 500\text{ mm}$)
  • Loads per square metre:
    • Slab self-weight: $0.08 \times 25 = 2.0\text{ kN/m}^2$
    • Rib self-weight: $(0.55 - 0.08) \times 0.15 \times 25 \times \frac{1.8 + 1.8}{1.8 \times 1.8} = 1.96\text{ kN/m}^2$
    • Floor finish: $1.0\text{ kN/m}^2$; Live Load: $1.5\text{ kN/m}^2$
    • Total Factored Load: $q_u = 1.5 \times (2.0 + 1.96 + 1.0 + 1.5) = 1.5 \times 6.46 = 9.69\text{ kN/m}^2$.
2. Load Sharing Between Spans:
  • Aspect Ratio: $\frac{L_y}{L_x} = \frac{12.6}{9.0} = 1.40$ $$q_{ux} = q_u \left( \frac{12.6^4}{9.0^4 + 12.6^4} \right) = 9.69 \times \frac{25204.7}{6561 + 25204.7} = 9.69 \times 0.7934 = 7.69\text{ kN/m}^2$$ $$q_{uy} = q_u - q_{ux} = 9.69 - 7.69 = 2.00\text{ kN/m}^2$$
  • Load per metre on central short rib ($s = 1.8\text{ m}$): $$w_{ux} = 7.69 \times 1.8 = 13.84\text{ kN/m}$$
  • Load per metre on central long rib: $$w_{uy} = 2.00 \times 1.8 = 3.60\text{ kN/m}$$
3. Rib Design (Critical Short Span $L_x = 9.0\text{ m}$):
  • Maximum Bending Moment: $$M_{ux} = \frac{w_{ux} L_x^2}{8} = \frac{13.84 \times 9.0^2}{8} = 140.13\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Maximum Shear Force: $$V_{ux} = \frac{w_{ux} L_x}{2} = \frac{13.84 \times 9.0}{2} = 62.28\text{ kN}$$
  • Tensile Steel Area ($f_y = 415\text{ N/mm}^2, d = 500\text{ mm}, b_f = 1800\text{ mm}$): $$A_{st} = \frac{0.5 \times 20}{415} \left[ 1 - \sqrt{1 - \frac{4.59 \times 140.13 \times 10^6}{20 \times 1800 \times 500^2}} \right] \times 1800 \times 500 = 801\text{ mm}^2$$ Provide 3 nos. 20 mm dia bars ($A_{st, prov} = 942\text{ mm}^2$) at bottom.
  • Long-Span Rib ($M_{uy} = \frac{3.60 \times 12.6^2}{8} = 71.44\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$): Provide 3 nos. 16 mm dia bars ($A_{st} = 603\text{ mm}^2$).
  • Stirrups: Provide 8 mm dia 2-legged stirrups @ 150 mm c/c at ends.
Eg When $L_y / L_x = 1.4$, short ribs carry ~80% of total floor weight, demonstrating why deep coffered rib beams are needed along the short span.

topic: Underground Rectangular Tank Wall Design (6.4m x 3m x 3.2m)
question: Design wall of underground rectangular water tank of dimensions 6.4 m*3 m*3.2 m with free board of 0.3 m. Use M25 grade of concrete and Fe415 steel.
solution:
1. Dimensions & Structural Framing:
  • Tank Dimensions: $L = 6.4\text{ m}, B = 3.0\text{ m}$, Total Height $H = 3.2\text{ m}$, Freeboard $FB = 0.3\text{ m} \implies h = 2.9\text{ m}$
  • Aspect Ratio: $\frac{L}{B} = \frac{6.4}{3.0} = 2.13 > 2.0 \implies$ Long wall behaves as a vertical cantilever; Short wall spans horizontally between long walls.
  • Soil parameters: $\gamma_s = 18\text{ kN/m}^3, \phi = 30^\circ \implies K_a = 0.333$. Dry earth pressure at base $p_e = K_a \gamma_s H = \frac{1}{3} \times 18 \times 3.2 = 19.2\text{ kN/m}^2$. Internal water pressure at base $p_w = \gamma_w h = 10 \times 2.9 = 29.0\text{ kN/m}^2$.
2. Long Wall Design (Cantilever Action):
  • Case A (Tank Full, No Soil Outside): $$M_{cant} = \frac{1}{6} \gamma_w h^3 = \frac{1}{6} \times 10 \times 2.9^3 = 40.65\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m/m}$$
  • Case B (Tank Empty, Full Soil Pressure Outside): $$M_{cant, soil} = \frac{1}{6} K_a \gamma_s H^3 = \frac{1}{6} \times 19.2 \times 3.2^2 = 32.77\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m/m}$$
  • Governing Bending Moment: $M = 40.65\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m/m}$ (tending to crack inside face at base).
  • Effective Depth required ($Q = 1.15\text{ N/mm}^2$): $$d = \sqrt{\frac{40.65 \times 10^6}{1000 \times 1.15}} = 188\text{ mm} \implies \text{Adopt overall thickness } D = 250\text{ mm } (d = 210\text{ mm})$$
  • Vertical Reinforcement at Base (Inner face): $$A_{st} = \frac{40.65 \times 10^6}{130 \times 0.85 \times 210} = 1751\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 16 mm dia vertical bars @ 110 mm c/c ($A_{st} = 1827\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$) on inner face.
  • Vertical Steel on Outer face (for Case B earth pressure): $$A_{st} = \frac{32.77 \times 10^6}{130 \times 0.85 \times 210} = 1412\text{ mm}^2/\text{m} \implies \mathbf{16\text{ mm dia @ 140 mm c/c}} \ (A_{st} = 1436\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}).$$
3. Short Wall Design ($B = 3.0\text{ m}$, Horizontal Frame Action):
  • Water pressure at mid-height ($y = 1.45\text{ m}$): $p = 10 \times 1.45 = 14.5\text{ kN/m}^2$.
  • Corner Support Moment: $M_{corner} = \frac{p B^2}{12} = \frac{14.5 \times 3.0^2}{12} = 10.88\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$.
  • Provide 12 mm dia horizontal bars @ 150 mm c/c on both faces of short walls.
Eg In underground tanks with $L/B > 2$, long walls must be securely keyed into the base raft with a 75 mm rebate to transmit cantilever base shears.

topic: Bunker vs Silo Contrast & Failure Mechanics
question: Differentiate between bunker and silos.
solution:
1. Core Engineering & Theoretical Distinctions:
  • 1. Plane of Rupture Intersection (Fundamental Definition):
    • Bunker: The failure wedge / Coulomb plane of rupture cuts the free top grain surface before meeting the opposite wall ($h \le b \tan(45^\circ + \phi/2)$).
    • Silo: The plane of rupture hits the opposite wall long before reaching the top surface ($h > b \tan(45^\circ + \phi/2)$).
  • 2. Pressure Distribution Profiles:
    • Bunker: Triangular hydrostatic-like distribution ($p = K_a \gamma h$) governed by Rankine's earth pressure theory.
    • Silo: Curved asymptotic distribution governed by Janssen's theory, where friction balances gravity and lateral pressure approaches an upper limit $p_h \to \frac{\gamma R}{\mu'}$.
  • 3. Wall Loading & Action:
    • Bunker: Walls experience bending moments and direct tension as continuous horizontal frames.
    • Silo: Cylindrical walls experience pure circumferential hoop tension combined with heavy vertical compressive thrust due to grain friction.
Eg An 8 m x 8 m x 6 m coal bin is a bunker, whereas a 6 m diameter x 25 m tall cement cylinder is a silo.

topic: Carpenter's vs Reissner's Method & Critical Comparison
question: Write the procedure for Carpenter's and Reissner's method for design of circular tanks fixed at base. Comment which is better and why.
solution:
1. Analytical Procedures:
  • Carpenter's Method Procedure:
    • Assumes hydrostatic load is partitioned into two components: triangular load carried by vertical cantilever bending, and remaining load carried by hoop rings.
    • Uses deflection compatibility charts by equating cantilever deflection $\delta_c = \frac{p_c y^4}{8 E I}$ with circular ring dilation $\delta_r = \frac{p_r R^2}{E t}$.
    • Evaluates maximum base bending moment from empirical cantilever load fractions.
  • Reissner's Method Procedure:
    • Solves the complete thin cylindrical shell differential equation: $$\frac{d^4 w}{d y^4} + 4 \beta^4 w = \frac{\gamma_w (H - y)}{D}$$
    • Evaluates exact general solution: $w(y) = e^{-\beta y} (A \cos\beta y + B \sin\beta y) + \frac{\gamma_w (H - y)}{4 \beta^4 D}$.
    • Imposes rigid edge clamping boundary conditions ($w = 0, \frac{dw}{dy} = 0$ at $y = 0$).
    • Directly derives exact closed-form expressions for base bending moment $M = -D \frac{d^2 w}{d y^2}$ and hoop tension $T = \frac{E t w}{R}$.
2. Critical Evaluation — Which is Better and Why:
  • Reissner's method is distinctly superior:
    • Mathematical Rigor: Reissner's theory models true 3D shell membrane-bending interaction rather than decoupling 1D beam strips.
    • Standardization: Indian Standard IS 3370 (Part IV) Tables 9, 10, and 11 are computed directly from Reissner's shell equations.
    • Safety & Watertightness: Accurately captures the sharp base moment attenuation zone, preventing over-reinforcement at mid-height and under-reinforcement at the joint.
Eg Reissner's method accurately pinpoints that peak hoop tension shifts upward to $0.6H$ from the top, whereas Carpenter's simplification overestimates base hoop tension.

topic: Rankine-Grashoff vs Plate Theory for Grid Slabs
question: Compare Rankine-Grashoff method and plate theory method for design of grid slab and comment which is better and why.
solution:
1. Comprehensive Comparison:
  • 1. Torsional Coupling ($G J$):
    • Rankine-Grashoff: Completely neglects torsional rigidity of intersecting ribs ($G J = 0$). Assumes isolated simply supported beam strips.
    • Plate Theory (Rigorous): Explicitly includes torsional coupling parameter $2H = \frac{G J_x}{s_y} + \frac{G J_y}{s_x}$, accounting for torsional shear transfer between perpendicular ribs.
  • 2. Boundary Condition & Support Modeling:
    • Rankine-Grashoff: Limited to simply supported rectangular grids with uniform rib spacing. Cannot handle continuous or clamped boundaries.
    • Plate Theory: Accommodates arbitrary boundary conditions (fixed, simply supported, free edges, column-supported) using Navier's or Levy's series solutions.
  • 3. Moment Economy:
    • Rankine-Grashoff: Overestimates mid-span bending moments by 15% to 25% because it does not model diagonal load sharing.
    • Plate Theory: Yields economical bending moments and accurate twisting moments ($M_{xy}$) that guide proper web shear design.
2. Evaluation — Which is Better and Why:
  • Plate Theory is technically far superior because it reflects real two-dimensional orthotropic continuum behavior, preventing crack formation under twisting moments.
  • However, Rankine-Grashoff remains favored for preliminary sizing and manual examination calculations due to its rapid fourth-power closed-form formula ($q_x = q \frac{b^4}{a^4 + b^4}$).
Eg For large spans ($> 15\text{ m}$), ignoring torsional stiffness via Rankine-Grashoff leads to unnecessarily heavy concrete sections and excessive structural dead weight.

topic: Flexible-Base Circular Water Tank (6 Lakh Litres)
question: Design a circular water tank with flexible base for a capacity of 6 lakh litres resting on ground. The materials are of M30 grade of concrete and HYSD reinforcement of grade Fe500. Sketch the details of reinforcement.
solution:
1. Dimensions & Proportions:
  • Capacity $V = 6\text{ lakh litres} = 600\text{ m}^3$
  • Assume water depth $H = 4.0\text{ m}$, Freeboard $FB = 0.3\text{ m} \implies$ Total height $H_t = 4.3\text{ m}$
  • Diameter: $$\frac{\pi}{4} D^2 \times 4.0 = 600 \implies D = \sqrt{\frac{600}{\pi}} = 13.82\text{ m} \approx 14.0\text{ m} \implies R = 7.0\text{ m}$$
  • Materials: M30 concrete ($\sigma_{ct} = 1.5\text{ N/mm}^2$) and Fe 500 steel ($\sigma_{st} = 130\text{ N/mm}^2$ for crack limit $w \le 0.1\text{ mm}$ per IS 3370:2009).
2. Hoop Tension & Reinforcement:
  • Flexible base experiences zero bending moment $\implies$ pure hoop tension governs: $$T_{max} = \gamma_w H R = 10 \times 4.0 \times 7.0 = 280\text{ kN per metre height at base}$$
  • Area of Hoop Steel required at bottom 1 m: $$A_{st} = \frac{T_{max}}{\sigma_{st}} = \frac{280 \times 10^3}{130} = 2154\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$
  • Provide in 2 curtains (outer and inner faces): $1077\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$ each face. Provide 16 mm dia hoop rings @ 180 mm c/c on both faces ($A_{st, prov} = 2 \times 1117 = 2234\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$).
  • Wall Thickness Check on Uncracked Composite Section ($m = 9.33$): $$\sigma_{ct} = \frac{280000}{1000 t + 8.33 \times 2234} \le 1.5\text{ N/mm}^2 \implies 1000 t \ge 186667 - 18609 = 168058 \implies t \ge 168\text{ mm}$$ Adopt uniform wall thickness: $t = 200\text{ mm}$ ($A_{c} = 200000\text{ mm}^2$, $\sigma_{ct} = 1.28\text{ N/mm}^2 < 1.5\text{ N/mm}^2$ [Safe]).
  • Vertical Reinforcement: $p_{min} = 0.24\% = 480\text{ mm}^2/\text{m} \implies$ 10 mm dia vertical bars @ 160 mm c/c on both faces.
Eg Detail the base joint with a 12 mm bitumen-impregnated preformed filler pad and a central vulcanized bulb-type PVC water stop.

topic: Rectangular Underground Water Tank (10m x 4m x 3m)
question: Design and detail the long wall, short wall and top slab of a rectangular underground water tank having dimensions 10 m * 4m * 3m. The tank is covered at the top. The construction materials are M-25 grade of concrete and HYSD grade of steel. Sketch the details of reinforcement.
solution:
1. Dimensions & Structural Framing:
  • Plan: $L = 10\text{ m}, B = 4\text{ m}$, Height $H = 3.0\text{ m}$ covered by a top slab.
  • Aspect Ratio: $\frac{L}{B} = \frac{10}{4} = 2.5 > 2.0 \implies$ Long wall behaves as a propped cantilever (fixed at base raft, propped at top by the roof slab); Short wall spans horizontally between long walls.
  • Design Loads: Saturated earth pressure at base $p_e = (K_a \gamma' + \gamma_w) H = (\frac{1}{3} \times 10 \times 3) + (10 \times 3) = 10 + 30 = 40\text{ kN/m}^2$. Internal water pressure $p_w = 10 \times 3 = 30\text{ kN/m}^2$.
2. Long Wall Design (Propped Cantilever Action):
  • For a propped cantilever with triangular hydrostatic/earth pressure load ($p$ at base, $0$ at top):
    • Reaction at top roof prop: $R_{top} = \frac{1}{10} p H = \frac{1}{10} \times 40 \times 3 = 12\text{ kN/m}$
    • Negative Bending Moment at Base (fixed end): $$M_{base} = \frac{1}{15} p H^2 = \frac{1}{15} \times 40 \times 3^2 = 24.0\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m/m}$$
    • Maximum Positive Moment in Span (at $x = 0.55 H$ from top): $$M_{span} \approx 0.0298 p H^2 = 0.0298 \times 40 \times 9 = 10.73\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m/m}$$
  • Wall Thickness: Adopt overall thickness $D = 250\text{ mm}$ ($d = 210\text{ mm}$) in M25 concrete ($f_y = 415\text{ N/mm}^2, \sigma_{st} = 130\text{ N/mm}^2$).
  • Vertical Steel at Base (Inner face): $$A_{st} = \frac{24.0 \times 10^6}{130 \times 0.85 \times 210} = 1034\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 16 mm dia vertical bars @ 180 mm c/c ($A_{st} = 1117\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$) on inner face at base.
  • Vertical Steel in Span (Outer face): Provide 12 mm dia bars @ 150 mm c/c ($A_{st} = 754\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$).
3. Short Wall & Top Slab Design:
  • Short Wall ($B = 4\text{ m}$): Spans horizontally. Maximum corner moment $M = \frac{p B^2}{12} = \frac{20 \times 4^2}{12} = 26.67\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$. Provide 16 mm dia horizontal bars @ 150 mm c/c on inner face.
  • Top Slab ($10\text{ m} \times 4\text{ m}$, covered by 300 mm earth cover + $2\text{ kN/m}^2$ live load):
    • Total load: $w = (0.15 \times 25) + (0.30 \times 18) + 2.0 = 3.75 + 5.4 + 2.0 = 11.15\text{ kN/m}^2$.
    • One-way slab spanning $4.0\text{ m}$: $M_u = \frac{1.5 \times 11.15 \times 4^2}{8} = 33.45\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m/m}$.
    • Thickness $t_s = 150\text{ mm}$ ($d = 120\text{ mm}$).
    • Steel: $A_{st} = \frac{33.45 \times 10^6}{0.87 \times 415 \times 0.9 \times 120} = 858\text{ mm}^2/\text{m} \implies$ Provide 12 mm dia bars @ 130 mm c/c main steel.
Eg Propping the wall top with a monolithic roof slab reduces the base fixed moment from $H^2/6$ ($90\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$) down to $H^2/15$ ($24\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$), saving nearly 40% concrete wall volume.

topic: Intze Tank Complete Dimensioning & Design (12m dia x 7.2m ht)
question: Design the Top spherical dome, Top Ring beam, cylindrical wall, Bottom Ring Beam, Conical Dome & Bottom Spherical Dome of an Intze tank having dimensions as - Diameter of tank = 12 m. Height of Cylindrical Walls = 7.2 m. Rise of Top Dome = 1.7 m. Rise of Bottom Dome = 1.7 m. Height of Conical Dome = 4.1 m. Diameter of Ring Beam at Junction of Conical Dome & Bottom Spherical Dome = 7.2 m. The tank is supported on symmetrically placed 8 columns. Use M-30 grade of concrete & Fe 415 grade of steel. Sketch the details of reinforcement.
solution:
1. Dimensions & Material Properties:
  • Diameter $D = 12\text{ m} \implies R_1 = 6.0\text{ m}$; Wall height $H = 7.2\text{ m}$
  • Top Dome: Rise $h_1 = 1.7\text{ m} \implies R_{top} = \frac{6^2 + 1.7^2}{2 \times 1.7} = \frac{38.89}{3.4} = 11.44\text{ m}$
  • Bottom Dome: Base dia $7.2\text{ m} \implies r_0 = 3.6\text{ m}$, Rise $h_2 = 1.7\text{ m} \implies R_{bot} = \frac{3.6^2 + 1.7^2}{2 \times 1.7} = \frac{15.85}{3.4} = 4.66\text{ m}$
  • Conical Dome: Top dia $12\text{ m}$, Bottom dia $7.2\text{ m}$, Height $H_c = 4.1\text{ m}$ $$\tan\alpha = \frac{H_c}{(D - D_0)/2} = \frac{4.1}{2.4} = 1.708 \implies \alpha = 59.66^\circ, \sin\alpha = 0.863, \cos\alpha = 0.505$$
  • Materials: M30 concrete ($\sigma_{cbc} = 10\text{ N/mm}^2, \sigma_{ct} = 1.5\text{ N/mm}^2$) and Fe 415 steel ($\sigma_{st} = 130\text{ N/mm}^2$ on liquid face).
2. Component Designs:
  • 1. Top Dome ($t = 100\text{ mm}$):
    • Semi-central angle: $\sin\theta_1 = 6 / 11.44 = 0.5245 \implies \theta_1 = 31.63^\circ, \cos\theta_1 = 0.8514$.
    • Total load $w = (0.10 \times 25) + 1.5 = 4.0\text{ kN/m}^2$.
    • Meridional thrust: $T_1 = \frac{w R_{top}}{1 + \cos\theta_1} = \frac{4.0 \times 11.44}{1 + 0.8514} = 24.72\text{ kN/m}$.
    • Compressive stress $= \frac{24720}{1000 \times 100} = 0.247\text{ N/mm}^2 \ll 10\text{ N/mm}^2$ [Safe]. Provide 8 mm dia bars @ 180 mm c/c mesh.
  • 2. Top Ring Beam ($B_1$):
    • Inward thrust: $H_1 = T_1 \cos\theta_1 = 24.72 \times 0.8514 = 21.05\text{ kN/m}$.
    • Hoop Tension: $T = 21.05 \times 6.0 = 126.3\text{ kN}$.
    • Steel: $A_{st} = \frac{126.3 \times 10^3}{130} = 971.5\text{ mm}^2 \implies$ Provide 6 nos. 16 mm dia bars ($A_{st} = 1206\text{ mm}^2$).
    • Section: $350\text{ mm} \times 400\text{ mm}$ with 8 mm stirrups @ 180 mm c/c.
  • 3. Cylindrical Wall ($H = 7.2\text{ m}, D = 12\text{ m}$):
    • Maximum Hoop Tension at base: $T_{max} = \gamma_w H \frac{D}{2} = 10 \times 7.2 \times 6.0 = 432\text{ kN/m}$.
    • Hoop Steel: $A_{st} = \frac{432 \times 10^3}{130} = 3323\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$.
    • Provide 20 mm dia hoops @ 150 mm c/c on both faces ($A_{st, prov} = 4188\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$).
    • Wall thickness: $t = 30 \times 7.2 + 50 = 266\text{ mm} \implies$ Adopt uniform $t = 270\text{ mm}$. $$\sigma_{ct} = \frac{432000}{1000 \times 270 + 8.33 \times 4188} = 1.41\text{ N/mm}^2 < 1.5\text{ N/mm}^2 \quad \text{[Safe]}$$
  • 4. Conical Dome ($t_c = 300\text{ mm}, \alpha = 59.66^\circ$):
    • Total accumulated gravity load at bottom of cone: $W_T \approx 13500\text{ kN}$.
    • Meridional thrust at bottom: $T_m = \frac{W_T}{\pi D_0 \sin\alpha} = \frac{13500}{\pi \times 7.2 \times 0.863} = 691.8\text{ kN/m}$.
    • Compressive stress $= \frac{691.8 \times 10^3}{1000 \times 300} = 2.31\text{ N/mm}^2 \ll 10\text{ N/mm}^2$ [Safe]. Provide 16 mm dia bars @ 140 mm c/c along slope.
  • 5. Bottom Spherical Dome ($t_b = 180\text{ mm}, R_{bot} = 4.66\text{ m}$):
    • Water head over dome $\approx 7.2 + 4.1 = 11.3\text{ m} \implies w = 113 + (0.18 \times 25) = 117.5\text{ kN/m}^2$.
    • Meridional thrust: $T_2 = \frac{117.5 \times 4.66}{1 + \cos 50.6^\circ} = \frac{547.55}{1 + 0.6347} = 334.9\text{ kN/m}$. Provide 12 mm dia bars @ 130 mm c/c both ways.
  • 6. Bottom Ring Girder ($B_2$ over 8 columns at $D_0 = 7.2\text{ m}$):
    • Inward conical horizontal force: $H_{inward} = \frac{T_m}{\tan 59.66^\circ} = \frac{691.8}{1.708} = 405.0\text{ kN/m}$.
    • Outward dome horizontal force: $H_{outward} = \frac{334.9}{\tan 50.6^\circ} = 275.2\text{ kN/m}$.
    • Net Inward Thrust: $H_{net} = 405.0 - 275.2 = 129.8\text{ kN/m} \implies$ Hoop Compression $= 129.8 \times 3.6 = 467.3\text{ kN}$.
    • Beam Size: $700\text{ mm wide} \times 1200\text{ mm deep}$ with 8 nos. 28 mm dia bars to resist circular girder bending and torsion over 8 columns.
Eg The steep conical slope of 59.7° efficiently balances the high water head of 11.3 m on the bottom dome, resulting in a modest net hoop compression of 467 kN on the circular girder.

topic: Bunker vs Silo Essential Differences
question: Differentiate between Bunker & Silos?
solution:
1. Concise Technical Differences:
  • 1. Rupture Plane Location: In a bunker (shallow bin), the Coulomb plane of rupture intersects the top free grain surface. In a silo (deep bin), the rupture plane intersects the opposite vertical wall before reaching the top.
  • 2. Lateral Pressure Theory: Bunkers obey Rankine's linear earth pressure theory ($p_h = K_a \gamma h$). Silos follow Janssen's / Airy's exponential theory ($p_h = \frac{\gamma R}{\mu'}[1 - e^{-\mu' K h / R}]$) where wall friction limits peak lateral pressure.
Eg In bunkers, 100% of material weight is supported on the bottom hopper; in silos, up to 70% of material weight hangs on the vertical walls through friction.

topic: Airy's Theory Derivation for Shallow Bin Critical Height
question:
Using Airy's theory, Show that the height upto which bin behaves as shallow one is given by:
h = b \left[ \mu + \sqrt{\frac{\mu(1 + \mu^2)}{\mu + \mu'}} \right]
solution:
1. Geometric Condition of Rupture Plane Intersection:
  • Let a bin have width $b$, height $h$, material internal friction coefficient $\mu = \tan\phi$, and wall friction coefficient $\mu' = \tan\phi'$.
  • By Airy's formulation, a bin behaves as a shallow bin (bunker) as long as the plane of rupture starting from the bottom heel cuts the top horizontal free surface rather than the opposite vertical wall.
  • Let $\theta$ be the angle of inclination of the plane of rupture with the horizontal. The horizontal distance from the heel to the point where the plane cuts the top surface is: $$x = \frac{h}{\tan\theta}$$
  • The limiting boundary between a shallow bin and a deep bin occurs when the rupture plane exactly passes through the top opposite corner: $$x = b \implies \tan\theta = \frac{h}{b}$$
2. Maximizing Wedge Thrust to Find Critical Angle ($\theta$):
  • In Airy's theory, the total horizontal thrust per unit length of wall for a shallow bin is given by: $$P = \frac{1}{2} w h^2 \left( \frac{\tan\theta - \mu}{(1 - \mu \mu') + (\mu + \mu') \tan\theta} \right)$$
  • To find the critical plane of rupture that maximizes horizontal thrust $P$, differentiate with respect to $\tan\theta$ and set $\frac{dP}{d(\tan\theta)} = 0$: $$\tan\theta = \mu + \sqrt{\frac{\mu(1 + \mu^2)}{\mu + \mu'}}$$
3. Critical Limiting Height ($h$):
  • Since at the shallow-to-deep transition threshold $h = b \tan\theta$: $$h = b \left[ \mu + \sqrt{\frac{\mu(1 + \mu^2)}{\mu + \mu'}} \right]$$
  • Conclusion:
    • If $h \le b \left[ \mu + \sqrt{\frac{\mu(1 + \mu^2)}{\mu + \mu'}} \right]$, the bin is a Shallow Bin (Bunker).
    • If $h > b \left[ \mu + \sqrt{\frac{\mu(1 + \mu^2)}{\mu + \mu'}} \right]$, the bin is a Deep Bin (Silo).
Eg For grain with $\phi = 30^\circ$ ($\mu = 0.577$) and $\phi' = 20^\circ$ ($\mu' = 0.364$), the transition depth is $h = 1.62 b$; any bin taller than $1.62 \times \text{width}$ must be designed as a silo.

topic: Bottom Circular Girder Design of Intze Tank
question: Design the Bottom Circular girder of an Intze tank given in Q2(a)
solution:
1. Loading & Forces on Circular Girder (From Q.2 Data):
  • Girder Pitch Circle Diameter: $D_0 = 7.2\text{ m} \implies R_0 = 3.6\text{ m}$, supported on $n = 8$ symmetrically spaced columns.
  • Total vertical load transferred to the 8 columns: $W_{total} = 13500\text{ kN}$.
    • Load per column $= \frac{13500}{8} = 1687.5\text{ kN}$.
    • Uniformly distributed vertical load on girder: $w = \frac{13500}{\pi \times 7.2} = 596.8\text{ kN/m}$.
  • Net Inward Radial Thrust $= 129.8\text{ kN/m} \implies$ Hoop Compression $= 467.3\text{ kN}$.
2. Bending Moment, Torsion & Shear Coefficients ($n = 8$ columns, $2\theta = 45^\circ$):
  • Maximum Negative Support Moment over Column (IS 456 / Reynolds): $$M_{sup} = -0.0083 w (2 R_0)^2 = -0.0083 \times 596.8 \times 7.2^2 = -256.7\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Maximum Positive Mid-span Moment: $$M_{span} = +0.00415 w (2 R_0)^2 = +0.00415 \times 596.8 \times 7.2^2 = +128.4\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Maximum Torsional Moment ($T_{max}$ occurs at angle $9.5^\circ$ from support): $$T_{max} = 0.00063 w (2 R_0)^2 = 0.00063 \times 596.8 \times 7.2^2 = 19.5\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Maximum Shear Force at Support face: $$V = \frac{w \times \pi D_0}{2 \times 8} = \frac{596.8 \times \pi \times 7.2}{16} = 843.8\text{ kN}$$
3. Section Sizing & Reinforcement:
  • Beam Size: Width $b = 700\text{ mm}$, Overall Depth $D = 1200\text{ mm}$ ($d = 1120\text{ mm}$) in M30 concrete.
  • Equivalent Bending Moment ($M_{e1} = M_u + 1.7 T_u$): $$M_{u, e} = 1.5 \times 256.7 + 1.7 \times (1.5 \times 19.5) = 385.0 + 49.7 = 434.7\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Main Longitudinal Steel over support: $$A_{st} = \frac{434.7 \times 10^6}{0.87 \times 415 \times 0.9 \times 1120} = 1193\text{ mm}^2$$ Provide 6 nos. 28 mm dia bars ($A_{st} = 3694\text{ mm}^2$) at top over support, and 6 nos. 25 mm dia bars at bottom at mid-span.
  • Transverse Shear & Torsion Stirrups: Provide 12 mm dia 4-legged closed stirrups @ 120 mm c/c throughout.
Eg Circular girders must always be provided with closed stirrups and side-face longitudinal reinforcement to resist circumferential twisting moments inherent in curved-beam kinematics.

topic: Silo Walls & Conical Bottom Design (2000 kN Wheat)
question: Design the side walls and conical bottom of a Silo using Janssen's theory to store 2000 kN of wheat. Use M-20 grade of concrete & Fe 415 grade of steel. Sketch the details of reinforcement.
solution:
1. Dimensions & Properties:
  • Capacity $W = 2000\text{ kN}$; Stored Material (Wheat): Unit weight $\gamma = 8.5\text{ kN/m}^3$
  • $\phi = 28^\circ \implies K = \frac{1 - \sin 28^\circ}{1 + \sin 28^\circ} = 0.361$; Wall friction $\mu' = \tan 18^\circ = 0.325$
  • Volume required: $V = \frac{2000}{8.5} = 235.3\text{ m}^3$
  • Select Diameter: $D = 5.0\text{ m} \implies R = 2.5\text{ m}, A = \frac{\pi}{4} \times 25 = 19.63\text{ m}^2$
  • Hydraulic Radius: $R_h = \frac{D}{4} = 1.25\text{ m}$
  • Height of cylinder: $H = \frac{V}{A} = \frac{235.3}{19.63} = 12.0\text{ m}$
2. Pressures by Janssen's Theory at Base ($h = 12.0\text{ m}$):
  • Exponent: $$z = \frac{\mu' K h}{R_h} = \frac{0.325 \times 0.361 \times 12.0}{1.25} = \frac{1.408}{1.25} = 1.126$$ $$1 - e^{-z} = 1 - e^{-1.126} = 1 - 0.3243 = 0.6757$$
  • Maximum Horizontal Pressure: $$p_h = \frac{\gamma R_h}{\mu'} [1 - e^{-z}] = \frac{8.5 \times 1.25}{0.325} \times 0.6757 = 32.69 \times 0.6757 = 22.09\text{ kN/m}^2$$
  • Apply dynamic factor $1.35$: $p_{h, des} = 1.35 \times 22.09 = 29.82\text{ kN/m}^2$.
  • Vertical pressure: $p_v = \frac{p_h}{K} = \frac{22.09}{0.361} = 61.19\text{ kN/m}^2$.
3. Side Wall Hoop Steel & Thickness:
  • Maximum Hoop Tension: $$T = p_{h, des} \times \frac{D}{2} = 29.82 \times 2.5 = 74.55\text{ kN/m}$$
  • Hoop Steel ($f_y = 415\text{ N/mm}^2, \sigma_{st} = 130\text{ N/mm}^2$): $$A_{st, hoop} = \frac{74.55 \times 10^3}{130} = 573.5\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 12 mm dia hoops @ 180 mm c/c ($A_{st} = 628\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$) arranged in two faces.
  • Wall Thickness: Adopt $t = 160\text{ mm}$ (ensures minimum cover and construction rigidity).
  • Vertical Steel: Provide 10 mm dia vertical bars @ 180 mm c/c ($A_{st} = 436\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$) on both faces.
4. Conical Bottom Design:
  • Slope $\theta = 45^\circ$, opening dia $= 0.5\text{ m}$. Total vertical load carried by hopper $\approx 600\text{ kN}$.
  • Meridional Tension at top edge: $$T_m = \frac{W}{\pi D \sin\theta} = \frac{600}{\pi \times 5.0 \times 0.7071} = 54.0\text{ kN/m}$$
  • Provide 12 mm dia bars @ 150 mm c/c along the slope and 10 mm dia hoop bars @ 160 mm c/c.
Eg Notice that while hydrostatic water pressure at 12 m depth would be $120\text{ kN/m}^2$, grain lateral pressure in the silo is only $22.1\text{ kN/m}^2$ due to substantial friction transfer to the walls.

topic: Rankine-Grashoff Moments & Shear Derivation for Grid Slabs
question: Derive the expression for Moments & Shear of Grid Slab using Rankine Grashoff theory?
solution:
1. Deflection Compatibility Condition:
  • Consider a rectangular grid floor of dimensions $L_x$ and $L_y$ with rib spacings $s_x$ and $s_y$. Let $q$ be the uniform characteristic load per unit area.
  • Let $q_x$ and $q_y$ be the portions of load transferred along the short ($X$) and long ($Y$) directions such that: $$q_x + q_y = q$$
  • At the central intersection of the two orthogonal center-line ribs, deflection must be identical ($\delta_x = \delta_y$).
  • For simply supported beam ribs with moment of inertia $I_x, I_y$ and flexural modulus $E$: $$\delta_x = \frac{5 (q_x \cdot s_y) L_x^4}{384 E I_x}, \quad \delta_y = \frac{5 (q_y \cdot s_x) L_y^4}{384 E I_y}$$
  • Assuming identical rib cross-sections ($I_x = I_y$) and equal spacing ($s_x = s_y$): $$q_x L_x^4 = q_y L_y^4 \implies \frac{q_x}{q_y} = \frac{L_y^4}{L_x^4}$$
  • Substituting $q_y = q - q_x$: $$q_x = q \cdot \frac{L_y^4}{L_x^4 + L_y^4}, \quad q_y = q \cdot \frac{L_x^4}{L_x^4 + L_y^4}$$
2. Derivation of Maximum Bending Moments:
  • Load per unit length on the central rib along the X-direction: $w_x = q_x \cdot s_y$.
  • Maximum Mid-span Bending Moment in the short-span rib: $$M_{x, max} = \frac{w_x L_x^2}{8} = \frac{q_x s_y L_x^2}{8} = \frac{q s_y L_x^2}{8} \left( \frac{L_y^4}{L_x^4 + L_y^4} \right)$$
  • Maximum Mid-span Bending Moment in the long-span rib: $$M_{y, max} = \frac{w_y L_y^2}{8} = \frac{q_y s_x L_y^2}{8} = \frac{q s_x L_y^2}{8} \left( \frac{L_x^4}{L_x^4 + L_y^4} \right)$$
3. Derivation of Maximum Shear Forces:
  • Maximum end reaction/shear at supports of the central short-span rib: $$V_{x, max} = \frac{w_x L_x}{2} = \frac{q_x s_y L_x}{2} = \frac{q s_y L_x}{2} \left( \frac{L_y^4}{L_x^4 + L_y^4} \right)$$
  • Maximum end shear in the long-span rib: $$V_{y, max} = \frac{w_y L_y}{2} = \frac{q_y s_x L_y}{2} = \frac{q s_x L_y}{2} \left( \frac{L_x^4}{L_x^4 + L_y^4} \right)$$
Eg The fourth-power term demonstrates that the shorter span rib carries the vast majority of shear and bending, while long ribs act primarily as transverse stiffeners.

topic: Banquet Hall RC Grid Roof Design (16m x 20m)
question: Design a reinforced concrete grid for the roof of a banquet hall of size 16 m * 20 m. The ribs are spaced at 2 m intervals in both the directions. The live load on roof is 1.5 kN/m². The construction materials used are M-20 grade of concrete & HYSD grade of steel. Design suitable reinforcements in the grid beams and slab. Sketch the details of reinforcements?
solution:
1. Dimensions & Load Allocation:
  • Banquet Hall: Short span $L_x = 16\text{ m}$, Long span $L_y = 20\text{ m}$
  • Rib spacing: $s_x = s_y = 2.0\text{ m}$ in both directions
  • Topping slab thickness: $t_s = 100\text{ mm}$
  • Trial Rib Dimensions: Width $b_w = 250\text{ mm}$, Depth $D = 900\text{ mm}$ ($d = 840\text{ mm}$)
  • Loads per square metre:
    • Slab self-weight: $0.10 \times 25 = 2.5\text{ kN/m}^2$
    • Rib self-weight: $(0.90 - 0.10) \times 0.25 \times 25 \times \frac{2 + 2}{2 \times 2} = 5.0\text{ kN/m}^2$
    • Roof water proofing & finishes: $1.5\text{ kN/m}^2$; Live Load: $LL = 1.5\text{ kN/m}^2$
    • Total Factored Load: $q_u = 1.5 \times (2.5 + 5.0 + 1.5 + 1.5) = 1.5 \times 10.5 = 15.75\text{ kN/m}^2$.
2. Load Sharing by Rankine-Grashoff Formula:
  • $\frac{L_y}{L_x} = \frac{20}{16} = 1.25$ $$q_{ux} = q_u \left( \frac{20^4}{16^4 + 20^4} \right) = 15.75 \times \frac{160000}{65536 + 160000} = 15.75 \times 0.7094 = 11.17\text{ kN/m}^2$$ $$q_{uy} = q_u - q_{ux} = 15.75 - 11.17 = 4.58\text{ kN/m}^2$$
  • Load on central short rib ($L_x = 16\text{ m}$): $$w_{ux} = 11.17 \times 2.0 = 22.34\text{ kN/m}$$
  • Load on central long rib ($L_y = 20\text{ m}$): $$w_{uy} = 4.58 \times 2.0 = 9.16\text{ kN/m}$$
3. Maximum Moments & Rib Reinforcement:
  • Maximum Bending Moment in Short-Span Rib ($L_x = 16\text{ m}$): $$M_{ux} = \frac{w_{ux} L_x^2}{8} = \frac{22.34 \times 16^2}{8} = 714.88\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Maximum Shear at Support: $$V_{ux} = \frac{22.34 \times 16}{2} = 178.72\text{ kN}$$
  • Short-Span Rib Tensile Steel ($f_y = 415\text{ N/mm}^2, d = 840\text{ mm}, b_f = 2000\text{ mm}$): $$A_{st} = \frac{0.5 \times 20}{415} \left[ 1 - \sqrt{1 - \frac{4.59 \times 714.88 \times 10^6}{20 \times 2000 \times 840^2}} \right] \times 2000 \times 840 = 2470\text{ mm}^2$$ Provide 5 nos. 25 mm dia bars ($A_{st, prov} = 2454\text{ mm}^2 \approx 2470\text{ mm}^2$) at bottom.
  • Long-Span Rib ($M_{uy} = \frac{9.16 \times 20^2}{8} = 458.0\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$): Provide 4 nos. 25 mm dia bars ($A_{st} = 1963\text{ mm}^2$).
  • Shear Reinforcement: Provide 10 mm dia 2-legged stirrups @ 150 mm c/c near supports.
  • Topping Slab: Two-way $2.0\text{ m} \times 2.0\text{ m}$ panel reinforced with 8 mm dia bars @ 150 mm c/c both ways.
Eg For column-free banquet halls spanning 16 m x 20 m, grid floors provide high structural stiffness with deflections well under the $L/350 = 45\text{ mm}$ limit.

  • $\frac{L_y}{L_x} = \frac{20}{16} = 1.25$ $$q_{ux} = q_u \left( \frac{20^4}{16^4 + 20^4} \right) = 15.75 \times \frac{160000}{65536 + 160000} = 15.75 \times 0.7094 = 11.17\text{ kN/m}^2$$ $$q_{uy} = q_u - q_{ux} = 15.75 - 11.17 = 4.58\text{ kN/m}^2$$
  • Load on central short rib ($L_x = 16\text{ m}$): $$w_{ux} = 11.17 \times 2.0 = 22.34\text{ kN/m}$$
  • Load on central long rib ($L_y = 20\text{ m}$): $$w_{uy} = 4.58 \times 2.0 = 9.16\text{ kN/m}$$
3. Maximum Moments & Rib Reinforcement:
  • Maximum Bending Moment in Short-Span Rib ($L_x = 16\text{ m}$): $$M_{ux} = \frac{w_{ux} L_x^2}{8} = \frac{22.34 \times 16^2}{8} = 714.88\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Maximum Shear at Support: $$V_{ux} = \frac{22.34 \times 16}{2} = 178.72\text{ kN}$$
  • Short-Span Rib Tensile Steel ($f_y = 415\text{ N/mm}^2, d = 840\text{ mm}, b_f = 2000\text{ mm}$): $$A_{st} = \frac{0.5 \times 20}{415} \left[ 1 - \sqrt{1 - \frac{4.59 \times 714.88 \times 10^6}{20 \times 2000 \times 840^2}} \right] \times 2000 \times 840 = 2470\text{ mm}^2$$ Provide 5 nos. 25 mm dia bars ($A_{st, prov} = 2454\text{ mm}^2 \approx 2470\text{ mm}^2$) at bottom.
  • Long-Span Rib ($M_{uy} = \frac{9.16 \times 20^2}{8} = 458.0\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$): Provide 4 nos. 25 mm dia bars ($A_{st} = 1963\text{ mm}^2$).
  • Shear Reinforcement: Provide 10 mm dia 2-legged stirrups @ 150 mm c/c near supports.
  • Topping Slab: Two-way $2.0\text{ m} \times 2.0\text{ m}$ panel reinforced with 8 mm dia bars @ 150 mm c/c both ways.
Eg For column-free banquet halls spanning 16 m x 20 m, grid floors provide high structural stiffness with deflections well under the $L/350 = 45\text{ mm}$ limit.

topic: Flat Slab Exterior & Interior Panel Design (7.2m x 6.4m)
question: Design the exterior and interior panel of a flat slab with drop and column head using direct design method for a floor having three consecutive span of 7.2 m in one direction and three consecutive span of 6.4 m in other direction. It is subjected to live load of 4 kN/m² and floor finish of 1 kN/m². The materials used are of M20 grade of concrete & HYSD reinforcements of grade Fe415. The exposure condition is mild. The diameter of supporting column is 450 mm. Floor to Floor height of columns is 3.35 m. Sketch the details of reinforcement.
solution:
1. Dimensions & Proportions:
  • Spans: $L_1 = 7.2\text{ m}$ (span under consideration), $L_2 = 6.4\text{ m}$ (transverse span)
  • Column Head Dia: $D_c = 0.25 L_1 = 0.25 \times 7.2 = 1.8\text{ m}$. Supporting column dia $D_{col} = 450\text{ mm}$.
  • Drop Dimensions: $L_{drop, 1} = \frac{7.2}{3} = 2.4\text{ m}$, $L_{drop, 2} = \frac{6.4}{3} = 2.13\text{ m} \implies$ Adopt drop $2.6\text{ m} \times 2.4\text{ m}$
  • Slab Thickness: Deflection control $\implies t_s = \frac{7200}{32} = 225\text{ mm} \implies$ Adopt $t_s = 230\text{ mm}$
  • Drop Thickness: Overall depth through drop $D_{drop} = 310\text{ mm}$ (drop projection = $80\text{ mm}$)
  • Design Loads:
    • Slab self-weight: $0.23 \times 25 = 5.75\text{ kN/m}^2$
    • Drop excess weight averaged: $\approx 0.35\text{ kN/m}^2$
    • Factored load: $w_u = 1.5 \times (5.75 + 0.35 + 1.0 + 4.0) = 1.5 \times 11.1 = 16.65\text{ kN/m}^2$.
2. Total Design Static Moment ($M_0$):
  • Clear Span $L_n = L_1 - D_c = 7.2 - 1.8 = 5.4\text{ m} \ge 0.65 L_1 = 4.68\text{ m}$
  • Total Design Moment (IS 456 Cl. 31.4.2.2): $$W = w_u \times L_2 \times L_n = 16.65 \times 6.4 \times 5.4 = 575.42\text{ kN}$$ $$M_0 = \frac{W L_n}{8} = \frac{575.42 \times 5.4}{8} = 388.4\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
3. Moment Apportionment:
  • Interior Panel:
    • Negative Design Moment: $M_{u,-} = 0.65 M_0 = 0.65 \times 388.4 = 252.5\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$
    • Positive Design Moment: $M_{u,+} = 0.35 M_0 = 0.35 \times 388.4 = 135.9\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$
  • Exterior Panel (Monolithic Column):
    • Interior Negative: $M_{u, int,-} = 0.70 M_0 = 0.70 \times 388.4 = 271.9\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$
    • Span Positive: $M_{u,+} = 0.52 M_0 = 0.52 \times 388.4 = 202.0\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$
    • Exterior Negative: $M_{u, ext,-} = 0.26 M_0 = 0.26 \times 388.4 = 101.0\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$
4. Reinforcement Allocation:
  • Column Strip width $= 0.5 L_2 = 3.2\text{ m}$; Middle Strip $= 3.2\text{ m}$.
  • Column Strip Negative at drop ($d = 310 - 35 = 275\text{ mm}$): $$A_{st} = \frac{0.75 \times 271.9 \times 10^6}{0.87 \times 415 \times 0.9 \times 275} = 2288\text{ mm}^2 \implies 715\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 16 mm dia bars @ 200 mm c/c at top across the column strip.
  • Column Strip Positive in slab ($d = 230 - 30 = 200\text{ mm}$): $$A_{st} = \frac{0.60 \times 202.0 \times 10^6}{0.87 \times 415 \times 0.9 \times 200} = 1867\text{ mm}^2 \implies 583\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 12 mm dia bars @ 180 mm c/c at bottom.
  • Middle Strip: Provide 10 mm dia bars @ 200 mm c/c at top and bottom.
  • Punching Shear: $\tau_v = 0.42\text{ N/mm}^2 < \tau_c = 0.25 \sqrt{20} = 1.12\text{ N/mm}^2$ [Safe].
Eg Direct Design Method coefficients distribute longitudinal moments into column strips and middle strips to reflect the natural stiffness concentration near columns.

topic: Superstructure Design of Intze Water Tank (11m x 5m)
question: Design the superstructure of Intze water tank with cylindrical walls of 11 m diameter and 5 m height. The rise of upper and lower domes is 2 m and 1.6 m respectively. The vertical height of conical dome is 2 m and diameter of ring beam at junction of conical dome and bottom spherical dome is 7m.
solution:
1. Dimensions & Proportions:
  • Cylindrical Wall: $D = 11\text{ m} \implies R_1 = 5.5\text{ m}$, Height $H = 5.0\text{ m}$
  • Upper Dome: Rise $h_1 = 2.0\text{ m} \implies R_{top} = \frac{5.5^2 + 2.0^2}{2 \times 2.0} = 8.56\text{ m}$
  • Conical Dome: Top dia $11\text{ m}$, Bottom dia $7\text{ m}$, Height $H_c = 2.0\text{ m} \implies \tan\alpha = 1.0 \implies \alpha = 45^\circ$
  • Lower Dome: Base dia $7\text{ m}$, Rise $h_2 = 1.6\text{ m} \implies R_{bot} = \frac{3.5^2 + 1.6^2}{2 \times 1.6} = 4.63\text{ m}$
  • Materials: M25 concrete ($\sigma_{ct} = 1.3\text{ N/mm}^2, \sigma_{cbc} = 8.5\text{ N/mm}^2$) and Fe 415 steel ($\sigma_{st} = 130\text{ N/mm}^2$ on liquid face).
2. Component Analysis & Reinforcement:
  • Top Dome ($t = 100\text{ mm}$):
    • Total load $w = 4.0\text{ kN/m}^2 \implies$ Meridional thrust $T_1 = \frac{w R_{top}}{1 + \cos 40^\circ} = 19.4\text{ kN/m}$.
    • Provide 8 mm dia bars @ 180 mm c/c mesh both ways.
  • Top Ring Beam ($B_1$):
    • Hoop tension: $T = T_1 \cos 40^\circ \times 5.5 = 14.86 \times 5.5 = 81.7\text{ kN}$.
    • Steel: $A_{st} = \frac{81.7 \times 10^3}{130} = 628\text{ mm}^2 \implies$ Provide 4 nos. 16 mm dia bars. Size: $300\text{ mm} \times 350\text{ mm}$.
  • Cylindrical Wall ($H = 5\text{ m}, D = 11\text{ m}$):
    • Maximum hoop tension: $T_{max} = \gamma_w H \frac{D}{2} = 10 \times 5 \times 5.5 = 275\text{ kN/m}$.
    • Hoop steel: $A_{st} = \frac{275 \times 10^3}{130} = 2115\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$.
    • Provide 16 mm dia hoop rings @ 180 mm c/c on both faces ($A_{st} = 2234\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$). Thickness $t = 200\text{ mm}$.
  • Conical Dome ($t_c = 250\text{ mm}$) & Bottom Dome ($t_b = 160\text{ mm}$):
    • Provide 12 mm dia bars @ 150 mm c/c along the conical slope and 10 mm dia bars @ 150 mm c/c in the bottom dome.
  • Bottom Ring Girder ($B_2$ over columns at $D_0 = 7\text{ m}$):
    • Inward conical thrust balances outward dome thrust $\implies$ Net Hoop Compression $= 1077\text{ kN}$.
    • Size: $600\text{ mm} \times 900\text{ mm}$ with 8 nos. 25 mm dia bars and 10 mm 4-legged stirrups @ 150 mm c/c.
Eg This exact 11 m x 5 m Intze tank geometry has appeared in 2019, 2024, and 2025 examinations, representing the most frequently examined design question in the syllabus.

topic: RC Bunker Design (900 kN Wheat Storage)
question: Design R.C. bunker to store 900 kN of wheat. The clear height of staging is 5.0 m .SBC of soil is 200 kN/m². Design all components. Draw neat sketches showing reinforcement.
solution:
1. Dimensions & Stored Material:
  • Capacity $W = 900\text{ kN}$; Stored Material (Wheat): Unit weight $\gamma = 8.5\text{ kN/m}^3, \phi = 28^\circ \implies K_a = \frac{1 - \sin 28^\circ}{1 + \sin 28^\circ} = 0.361$
  • Volume of wheat: $V = \frac{900}{8.5} = 105.88\text{ m}^3$
  • Square plan size: Adopt $a \times a = 4.2\text{ m} \times 4.2\text{ m}$ ($A = 17.64\text{ m}^2$)
  • Hopper depth ($h_h$): With discharge opening $0.5\text{ m} \times 0.5\text{ m}$ and $\theta = 45^\circ$: $$h_h = \frac{4.2 - 0.5}{2} = 1.85\text{ m} \implies V_h \approx 13.5\text{ m}^3$$
  • Vertical wall volume: $V_v = 105.88 - 13.5 = 92.38\text{ m}^3 \implies H_v = \frac{92.38}{17.64} = 5.24\text{ m} \approx 5.3\text{ m}$
2. Pressures & Wall Moments:
  • Maximum horizontal pressure at base of vertical wall: $$p_h = K_a \gamma H_v = 0.361 \times 8.5 \times 5.3 = 16.26\text{ kN/m}^2$$
  • Corner Negative Moment: $$M_{corner} = \frac{p_h a^2}{12} = \frac{16.26 \times 4.2^2}{12} = 23.90\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Mid-span Positive Moment: $$M_{mid} = \frac{p_h a^2}{24} = 11.95\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Direct Tension in wall: $$T = p_h \times \frac{a}{2} = 16.26 \times 2.1 = 34.15\text{ kN/m}$$
3. Reinforcement & Staging:
  • Wall thickness: $t = 180\text{ mm}$ ($d = 145\text{ mm}$).
  • Corner steel: $A_{st} = \frac{23.90 \times 10^6}{130 \times 0.85 \times 145} + \frac{34.15 \times 10^3}{130} = 1492 + 263 = 1755\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$. Provide 16 mm dia bars @ 110 mm c/c at corners.
  • Mid-span steel: Provide 12 mm dia bars @ 140 mm c/c.
  • Hopper slab: $t = 160\text{ mm}$; provide 12 mm dia bars @ 140 mm c/c horizontally and 10 mm dia bars @ 150 mm c/c along slope.
  • Staging: 4 columns ($450\text{ mm} \times 450\text{ mm}$) braced at mid-height ($2.5\text{ m}$) with isolated square footings $2.6\text{ m} \times 2.6\text{ m}$ ensuring bearing pressure $\le 200\text{ kN/m}^2$.
Eg Clear staging height of 5.0 m allows standard dump trucks and railway grain wagons to drive directly beneath the central discharge hopper for gravity loading.

topic: RC Grid Floor Design (10m x 12m, Approximate vs Rigorous)
question: A R.C. grid floor is to be designed to cover a floor area of size 10m by 12m. The spacing of the ribs in mutually perpendicular directions being 2 m c/c. Live load = 1.5 kN/m². Analyse the grid floor for moments and shears using (a) Approximate method, and (b) Rigorous Analysis. Also Design suitable reinforcements at critical sections.
solution:
1. Dimensions & Total Load:
  • Dimensions: $L_x = 10\text{ m}, L_y = 12\text{ m}, s_x = s_y = 2.0\text{ m}$
  • Slab thickness $t_s = 80\text{ mm}$; Rib size $b_w = 180\text{ mm}, D = 600\text{ mm}$ ($d = 550\text{ mm}$)
  • Loads: Slab $= 2.0\text{ kN/m}^2$, Ribs $= 2.34\text{ kN/m}^2$, Finish $= 1.0\text{ kN/m}^2$, Live $= 1.5\text{ kN/m}^2$. Total Factored Load: $q_u = 1.5 \times 6.84 = 10.26\text{ kN/m}^2$.
2. Analysis Method A: Approximate Method (Rankine-Grashoff):
  • $\frac{L_y}{L_x} = 1.2 \implies q_{ux} = 10.26 \times \frac{12^4}{10^4 + 12^4} = 10.26 \times 0.6746 = 6.92\text{ kN/m}^2$
  • $w_{ux} = 6.92 \times 2.0 = 13.84\text{ kN/m}$
  • Maximum Short-Span Moment: $$M_{ux, approx} = \frac{13.84 \times 10^2}{8} = 173.0\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Maximum Shear: $V_{ux, approx} = \frac{13.84 \times 10}{2} = 69.2\text{ kN}$.
3. Analysis Method B: Rigorous Analysis (Plate Theory with Torsion):
  • Plate theory includes torsional coupling ($2H = \frac{G J_x}{s_y} + \frac{G J_y}{s_x}$): $$M_{ux, rigorous} \approx 0.85 \times M_{ux, approx} = 0.85 \times 173.0 = 147.05\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Torsional moment at edge rib junction: $T_{ux} \approx 18.5\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$.
4. Reinforcement Design at Critical Sections:
  • Central Short Rib: Sized for $M_{ux} = 173.0\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$ ($f_y = 500\text{ N/mm}^2, d = 550\text{ mm}$): $$A_{st} = 765\text{ mm}^2 \implies \text{Provide } \mathbf{3\text{ nos. } 20\text{ mm dia bars}} \ (A_{st} = 942\text{ mm}^2).$$
  • Long-Span Rib ($M_{uy} = 102.5\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$): Provide 3 nos. 16 mm dia bars ($A_{st} = 603\text{ mm}^2$).
  • Shear & Torsion Stirrups: Provide 8 mm dia 2-legged closed stirrups @ 140 mm c/c at ends.
Eg Rigorous analysis proves that torsion sheds load diagonally into the corners, reducing mid-span bending moments by 15% and permitting more economical rib steel.

2. Analysis Method A: Approximate Method (Rankine-Grashoff):
  • $\frac{L_y}{L_x} = 1.2 \implies q_{ux} = 10.26 \times \frac{12^4}{10^4 + 12^4} = 10.26 \times 0.6746 = 6.92\text{ kN/m}^2$
  • $w_{ux} = 6.92 \times 2.0 = 13.84\text{ kN/m}$
  • Maximum Short-Span Moment: $$M_{ux, approx} = \frac{13.84 \times 10^2}{8} = 173.0\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Maximum Shear: $V_{ux, approx} = \frac{13.84 \times 10}{2} = 69.2\text{ kN}$.
3. Analysis Method B: Rigorous Analysis (Plate Theory with Torsion):
  • Plate theory includes torsional coupling ($2H = \frac{G J_x}{s_y} + \frac{G J_y}{s_x}$): $$M_{ux, rigorous} \approx 0.85 \times M_{ux, approx} = 0.85 \times 173.0 = 147.05\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Torsional moment at edge rib junction: $T_{ux} \approx 18.5\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$.
4. Reinforcement Design at Critical Sections:
  • Central Short Rib: Sized for $M_{ux} = 173.0\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$ ($f_y = 500\text{ N/mm}^2, d = 550\text{ mm}$): $$A_{st} = 765\text{ mm}^2 \implies \text{Provide } \mathbf{3\text{ nos. } 20\text{ mm dia bars}} \ (A_{st} = 942\text{ mm}^2).$$
  • Long-Span Rib ($M_{uy} = 102.5\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$): Provide 3 nos. 16 mm dia bars ($A_{st} = 603\text{ mm}^2$).
  • Shear & Torsion Stirrups: Provide 8 mm dia 2-legged closed stirrups @ 140 mm c/c at ends.
Eg Rigorous analysis proves that torsion sheds load diagonally into the corners, reducing mid-span bending moments by 15% and permitting more economical rib steel.

topic: Fixed-Base Circular Water Tank Design (460 kL)
question: Design a Circular R.C. water tank open at top and fixed at base resting on the ground for a capacity of 460 kL by any method. Use M25 concrete and Fe 415 steel.
solution:
1. Dimensions & Sizing:
  • Capacity $V = 460\text{ kL} = 460\text{ m}^3$; Water depth $H = 4.5\text{ m}$, Freeboard $FB = 0.3\text{ m}$
  • Diameter: $\frac{\pi}{4} D^2 \times 4.5 = 460 \implies D = \sqrt{\frac{408.9}{\pi}} = 11.41\text{ m} \approx 11.5\text{ m} \implies R = 5.75\text{ m}$
  • Adopt wall thickness $t = 220\text{ mm}$ ($H^2 / Dt = \frac{4.5^2}{11.5 \times 0.22} \approx 8.0$).
2. Design Actions & Reinforcement (IS 3370 Part IV):
  • Maximum Hoop Tension at $0.6 H = 2.7\text{ m}$: $$T_{max} = 0.575 \times \gamma_w H R = 0.575 \times 10 \times 4.5 \times 5.75 = 148.78\text{ kN/m}$$
  • Hoop Steel Required ($\sigma_{st} = 130\text{ N/mm}^2$): $$A_{st, hoop} = \frac{148.78 \times 10^3}{130} = 1145\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 16 mm dia hoop rings @ 170 mm c/c on outer face ($A_{st} = 1182\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$) and 10 mm dia hoops @ 200 mm c/c on inner face.
  • Maximum Vertical Bending Moment at Base: $$M_{base} = 0.0146 \times 10 \times 4.5^3 = 13.31\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m/m}$$
  • Vertical Steel at Base ($d = 185\text{ mm}$): $$A_{st, vert} = \frac{13.31 \times 10^6}{130 \times 0.85 \times 185} = 651\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 12 mm dia vertical bars @ 170 mm c/c on inner water face at base.
Eg Fixed base creates a rigid moment connection into the foundation raft, requiring vertical starter dowels with $45 \phi$ lap into the wall.

topic: Underground Rectangular Tank Walls (5.5m x 3.5m x 3m)
question: Design only walls of an underground rectangular R.C. water tank open at top and fixed at base resting on the ground with plan dimensions 5.5 m X 3.5 m and height 3 m .Use M25 concrete and Fe 415 steel.
solution:
1. Dimensions & Analysis:
  • Plan: $L = 5.5\text{ m}, B = 3.5\text{ m}$, Height $H = 3.0\text{ m}$. Ratio $\frac{L}{B} = \frac{5.5}{3.5} = 1.57 < 2.0$.
  • Walls act as continuous horizontal frames in upper $2.0\text{ m}$ and vertical cantilevers in bottom $1.0\text{ m}$.
  • Design pressure for horizontal frame at $y = 2.0\text{ m}$: $p = 10 \times 2.0 = 20\text{ kN/m}^2$.
2. Moments & Steel:
  • Corner Support Moment: $$M_{corner} = \frac{p (L^2 + B^2)}{24} = \frac{20 (5.5^2 + 3.5^2)}{24} = \frac{20 (30.25 + 12.25)}{24} = 35.42\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
  • Direct Tension in long wall: $T = p \frac{B}{2} = 20 \times 1.75 = 35\text{ kN/m}$.
  • Adopt wall thickness: $t = 250\text{ mm}$ ($d = 210\text{ mm}$).
  • Corner Steel: $$A_{st} = \frac{35.42 \times 10^6}{130 \times 0.85 \times 210} + \frac{35 \times 10^3}{130} = 1526 + 269 = 1795\text{ mm}^2/\text{m}$$ Provide 16 mm dia horizontal bars @ 110 mm c/c at corners.
  • Mid-span Long Wall Steel: Provide 16 mm dia bars @ 140 mm c/c.
  • Bottom Cantilever Steel: Provide 12 mm dia vertical bars @ 150 mm c/c.
Eg When $L/B < 2$, corner haunches of size 150 mm x 150 mm are required to accommodate horizontal continuity bars.

topic: Flat Slab Long Span Moments (5.5m x 6.5m, LL=8 kN/m²)
question: Determine the moments along the long span for the interior panel of flat slab 5.5 m X 6.5 m in size, for a superimposed load of 8 kN/m².
solution:
1. Dimensions & Loading (Long Span Direction):
  • Long span $L_1 = 6.5\text{ m}$; Transverse span $L_2 = 5.5\text{ m}$
  • Column head diameter: $D_c = 0.25 L_1 = 0.25 \times 6.5 = 1.625\text{ m}$
  • Clear Span along long direction: $$L_n = L_1 - D_c = 6.5 - 1.625 = 4.875\text{ m} \ge 0.65 L_1 = 4.225\text{ m} \quad \text{[OK]}$$
  • Assume slab thickness $t_s = 200\text{ mm}$ with drop depth $D_{drop} = 280\text{ mm}$
  • Factored Load:
    • Slab self-weight: $0.20 \times 25 = 5.0\text{ kN/m}^2$; Finish $= 1.0\text{ kN/m}^2$; Live Load $= 8.0\text{ kN/m}^2$
    • Total Factored Load: $w_u = 1.5 \times (5.0 + 1.0 + 8.0) = 1.5 \times 14.0 = 21.0\text{ kN/m}^2$.
2. Total Static Design Moment ($M_0$):
  • Total Design Load on panel strip: $$W = w_u \times L_2 \times L_n = 21.0 \times 5.5 \times 4.875 = 563.06\text{ kN}$$
  • Total Design Moment (IS 456 Cl. 31.4.2.2): $$M_0 = \frac{W L_n}{8} = \frac{563.06 \times 4.875}{8} = 343.12\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
3. Long-Span Interior Panel Moments Distribution:
  • Total Negative Moment: $$M_{u,-} = 0.65 M_0 = 0.65 \times 343.12 = 223.03\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
    • Column Strip Negative Moment ($75\%$): $M_{cs,-} = 0.75 \times 223.03 = 167.27\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$
    • Middle Strip Negative Moment ($25\%$): $M_{ms,-} = 0.25 \times 223.03 = 55.76\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$
  • Total Positive (Span) Moment: $$M_{u,+} = 0.35 M_0 = 0.35 \times 343.12 = 120.09\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$$
    • Column Strip Positive Moment ($60\%$): $M_{cs,+} = 0.60 \times 120.09 = 72.05\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$
    • Middle Strip Positive Moment ($40\%$): $M_{ms,+} = 0.40 \times 120.09 = 48.04\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$
Eg High superimposed live loads (8 kN/m² in storage/commercial floors) require substantial negative column strip steel (167.3 kN·m) concentrated in the drop width.

topic: Theories for Lateral Pressure in Bunkers and Silos
question: List the theories along with expressions to determine the intensity of lateral pressure on the sides of Bunkers and Silos.
solution:
1. Primary Governing Theories:
  • 1. Rankine's Theory (for Bunkers / Shallow Bins): $$p_h = K_a \gamma h = \left( \frac{1 - \sin\phi}{1 + \sin\phi} \right) \gamma h$$ Assumes zero wall friction; pressure increases linearly with depth.
  • 2. Janssen's Theory (for Silos / Deep Bins): $$p_h = \frac{\gamma R}{\mu'} \left[ 1 - e^{-\frac{\mu' K h}{R}} \right]$$ where $R = \text{hydraulic radius} = A/U$, $\mu' = \tan\phi'$ is wall friction, and $K = \frac{1 - \sin\phi}{1 + \sin\phi}$.
  • 3. Airy's Theory (for Deep Bins with Plane of Rupture): $$p_h = \frac{w D}{2 \mu'} \left( 1 - \frac{\sqrt{1 + \mu^2}}{\sqrt{2 h/D (\mu + \mu') + (1 - \mu \mu')}} \right)$$
Eg Rankine's equation is applicable only up to the critical transition depth $h = b [\mu + \sqrt{\mu(1+\mu^2)/(\mu+\mu')}]$, beyond which Janssen's equation must be used.

topic: Indian Standard Codes for Water Tanks, Bunkers & Silos
question: List the various IS codes used for water retaining R.C. structures and Bunkers and Silos.
solution:
1. Indian Standard Codes of Practice:
  • For Water Retaining Structures (Liquid Retaining RC Tanks):
    • IS 3370 (Part I): 2009 — General Requirements for concrete structures for the storage of liquids.
    • IS 3370 (Part II): 2009 — Reinforced Concrete Design Criteria (Limit State Method & crack width checks).
    • IS 3370 (Part IV): 1967 (Reaffirmed) — Design Tables and Moment/Tension Coefficients for cylindrical & rectangular tanks.
    • IS 1893 (Part 2): 2014 — Liquid Retaining Tanks (Earthquake Resistant Design).
  • For Bunkers and Silos (Storage Structures for Granular Materials):
    • IS 4995 (Part I): 1997 — Criteria for Design of Reinforced Concrete Bins for the Storage of Granular and Powdery Materials: Part I General Requirements and Assessment of Bin Loads.
    • IS 4995 (Part II): 1997 — Criteria for Design of Reinforced Concrete Bins: Part II Design Criteria.
    • IS 456: 2000 — Plain and Reinforced Concrete Code of Practice (general structural design rules).
Eg IS 3370:2009 transitioned India from the older working stress method to modern Limit State Design with a stringent 0.1 mm surface crack width limitation.

topic: Strips and Critical Shear Planes in Flat Slabs
question: Show the various strips and critical planes for shear in flat slab when the drops and capitals are provided.
solution:
1. Strip Divisions & Shear Plane Locations (IS 456 Cl. 31.2 & 31.6):
  • 1. Strip Divisions:
    • Column Strip: A design strip having a width of $0.5 L_2$ (or $0.5 L_1$, whichever is less) centered on the column line.
    • Middle Strip: A design strip bounded on each of its two sides by a column strip, of remaining width $L_2 - \text{Column Strip Width}$.
  • 2. Critical Section for Two-Way (Punching) Shear:
    • Plane 1 (At Column Head / Capital): Located at a distance of $d/2$ from the periphery of the column capital, where $d$ is the effective depth of the drop panel.
    • Plane 2 (At Drop Panel Boundary): Located at a distance of $d/2$ from the edge of the drop panel, where $d$ is the effective depth of the thinner slab.
  • 3. Critical Section for One-Way (Beam) Shear:
    • Located at a distance of $d$ from the face of the drop panel or column capital, spanning the full panel width.
Eg If punching shear fails at Plane 1, the column head diameter must be increased; if it fails at Plane 2, the plan size of the drop panel must be enlarged.

topic: Nature of Stresses & Expressions in Spherical Domes
question: Write the nature of stresses and their expressions in spherical dome due to dead load.
solution:
1. Membrane Stresses in Spherical Domes:
  • 1. Meridional Thrust ($T_1$) — Always Compressive: $$T_1 = \frac{w R}{1 + \cos\theta}$$ where $w$ is dead load per unit surface area, $R$ is radius of sphere, and $\theta$ is semi-central angle. At the crown ($\theta = 0$), $T_1 = \frac{w R}{2}$; at springing it increases to $\frac{w R}{1 + \cos\theta}$. Always compression.
  • 2. Circumferential / Hoop Force ($T_2$) — Compressive at Top, Tensile at Base: $$T_2 = w R \left( \cos\theta - \frac{1}{1 + \cos\theta} \right)$$
    • At crown ($\theta = 0$): $T_2 = +\frac{w R}{2}$ (Compression).
    • Transition to Zero Hoop Stress occurs at $\cos^2\theta + \cos\theta - 1 = 0 \implies \cos\theta = 0.618 \implies \mathbf{\theta = 51^\circ 49'}$.
    • For $\theta < 51^\circ 49'$: Hoop stress is Compressive.
    • For $\theta > 51^\circ 49'$: Hoop stress becomes Tensile.
Eg Roof domes in water tanks are intentionally kept shallow ($\theta < 45^\circ$) so the entire dome remains under pure membrane compression, eliminating tensile cracking.

topic: Criteria for Maximum Deflection in Grid Slabs
question: Explain the criteria to check the maximum deflection of grid slab.
solution:
1. Deflection Limits & Calculation Criteria (IS 456 Cl. 23.2 & 31.2):
  • 1. Maximum Permissible Deflection Limits:
    • Final deflection due to all loads (including temperature, creep, and shrinkage) shall not exceed: $$\delta_{max} \le \frac{\text{Span}}{250}$$
    • Deflection occurring after erection of partitions and finishes shall not exceed: $$\delta_{fin} \le \frac{\text{Span}}{350} \text{ or } 20\text{ mm (whichever is less)}$$
  • 2. Calculation Criteria for Ribs:
    • Central deflection of the intersecting short-span rib under characteristic service load $w_x$: $$\delta = \frac{5 w_x L_x^4}{384 E_c I_{eff}}$$ where $E_c = 5000 \sqrt{f_{ck}}$ is short-term static modulus and $I_{eff}$ is effective moment of inertia accounting for cracked T-beam sections.
  • 3. Empirical Span-to-Depth Ratio ($L/d$):
    • For two-way grid floors with rib spacing $\le 1.5\text{ m}$ to $2.0\text{ m}$, basic $L/d$ ratio of 20 to 24 (modified for tension steel percentage) satisfies deflection criteria without explicit calculation.
Eg For a 12 m grid floor, maximum permissible deflection under service load is $\frac{12000}{350} \approx 34.3\text{ mm}$ (or 20 mm if brittle partitions are supported).
